children.title: Dimensional-Lineality Reduction Calculus
children.top_down_role: Reductions required for empty-interior, nonpointed, or non-full-dimensional domains.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine-Hull and Lineality Reduction of Barrier Domains
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\subset E\) be a nonempty closed convex set, \(A=\operatorname{aff}Q\), \(V=A-A\), and \(L=\operatorname{lin}Q\subset V\). Let \(\pi:V\to V/L\) be the quotient map and choose \(x_0\in\operatorname{ri}Q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional reduction used before applying full-dimensional pointed-domain barrier theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The dimensional-lineality reduction of \(Q\) is the two-stage replacement \[Q\subset E\longmapsto Q_A=Q-x_0\subset V\longmapsto\widehat Q=\pi(Q_A)\subset V/L.\] The first stage replaces ambient interior by relative interior: \(\operatorname{int}_V(Q_A)=\operatorname{ri}_E(Q)-x_0\neq\varnothing\). The second removes all two-sided recession directions: \(\operatorname{lin}\widehat Q=\{0\}\). A reduced barrier is a function \(\widehat F:\operatorname{int}\widehat Q\to\mathbb R\); its pullback \(F(x)=\widehat F(\pi(x-x_0))\) is constant on cosets parallel to \(L\) and has Hessian kernel containing \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First restrict a non-full-dimensional convex set to its affine hull, where its relative interior becomes an ordinary interior. Then quotient the direction space by the lineality subspace. The resulting closed convex set is full-dimensional in its own space and pointed. A barrier on the quotient pulls back to a barrier that is constant along lineality directions and consequently has a degenerate Hessian there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat Q=\pi(Q-x_0)\) has nonempty interior in \(V/L\) and no nonzero lineality, while \(F=\widehat F\circ\pi(\cdot-x_0)\) satisfies \(D^2F(x)[\ell,\ell]=0\) for every \(\ell\in L\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Choosing a linear complement \(V=L\oplus W\) identifies \(V/L\) with \(W\) and identifies \(\widehat Q\) with a pointed cross-section of \(Q-x_0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(Q\) is full-dimensional and pointed, then \(V=E\), \(L=\{0\}\), and no reduction occurs.
For an affine subspace \(Q=A\), the quotient set is a singleton and contains no nontrivial barrier geometry.
immediate_consequences_latex: Inverse-Hessian formulas should be applied on the reduced space, not along removed lineality directions.
Affine pullbacks can reconstruct the original representation after analysis on the quotient.
boundary_notes: A precise supplied source for the complete affine-hull-plus-quotient calculus was not located.
Quotienting lineality is distinct from projecting away arbitrary recession directions.

notation.meaning: direction space of the affine hull
quotient map onto the lineality-free space

The mathematical reduction is standard convex geometry, but the supplied locators do not support its complete barrier formulation.

children.title: Lineality-Space Reduction
children.top_down_role: Removal of directions along which the domain contains complete affine lines.

assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space, \(L\subseteq E\) is a linear subspace, and \(D\subseteq E\) satisfies \(D+L=D\).
\(F:D\to\mathbb{R}\) is smooth and satisfies \(F(x+\ell)=F(x)\) for every \(x\in D\) and \(\ell\in L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a unique function \(\widetilde F:\pi(D)\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(F=\widetilde F\circ\pi\), and the Hessian of \(F\) factors through the quotient with \(L\) contained in its kernel.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact fiber invariance is required for descent. The quotient Hessian is nondegenerate only under the additional condition that the original Hessian has no kernel beyond the lineality space.

source_refs.locator: 3.1 General convex functions p. 111
source_refs.source_title: Introductory Lectures on Convex Optimization: A Basic Course

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\subseteq E\) satisfy \(D+L=D\), and let \(\pi:E\to E/L\) be the quotient map. If \(F(x+\ell)=F(x)\) for every \(x\in D\) and \(\ell\in L\), then there is a unique function \(\widetilde F:\pi(D)\to\mathbb{R}\) such that \(F=\widetilde F\circ\pi\) on \(D\). Every derivative of \(F\) vanishes when one of its arguments lies in \(L\), and its Hessian is the pullback of the Hessian of \(\widetilde F\). The quotient Hessian is positive definite precisely when the kernel of \(\nabla^2F(x)\) is exactly \(L\) at every \(x\in D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function constant along the fibers of a lineality quotient descends uniquely to the quotient, and its Hessian descends there; nondegeneracy requires that lineality account for the entire original Hessian kernel.
knowledge_statements.title: Lineality-Space Reduction

children.title: Pointed Quotient Domains
children.top_down_role: Quotient-domain geometry obtained after eliminating lineality.

assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional vector space.
\(L=K\cap(-K)\) is its lineality space and \(\pi:E\to E/L\) is the quotient map.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quotienting by all lineality produces the canonical pointed cone supporting nondegenerate conic barrier geometry.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L=K\cap(-K)\) and \(\overline K=\pi(K)\subseteq E/L\). Then \(\overline K\) is a convex cone and is pointed, namely \(\overline K\cap(-\overline K)=\{0\}\). Moreover, \(\pi(\operatorname{ri}K)=\operatorname{ri}\overline K\). Hence any function on \(\operatorname{ri}K\) that is constant on the cosets of \(L\) descends uniquely to \(\operatorname{ri}\overline K\); when the descended function is a self-concordant barrier, its parameter and derivative inequalities are computed on the quotient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quotienting a closed convex cone by its entire lineality space yields a pointed cone and carries relative interiors onto relative interiors.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Valid affine reduction must supply coordinates for the relevant affine hull, and valid quotient reduction must respect quotient fibers. Let \(D=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}\), let \(q:D\to(0,[?25l∞)\) be defined by \(q(x,y)=x\), and let \(F(x,y)=-\log x\), the pullback under \(q\) of the logarithmic barrier on \((0,[?25l∞)\). For the affine embedding \(T:\mathbb{R}\to D\) defined by \(T(t)=(1,t)\), one has \((F\circ T)(t)=0\), so the pullback Hessian vanishes. Thus a slice contained in one quotient fiber loses the nondegenerate quotient barrier geometry and cannot replace affine-hull or lineality reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A slice lying inside a quotient fiber can turn a nondegenerate quotient barrier into a constant function, so faithful affine coordinates and exact quotient compatibility are essential.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hierarchy of General, Logarithmically Homogeneous, and Self-Scaled Barriers
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\subset E\) be a closed pointed convex cone with nonempty interior. Let \(F:\operatorname{int}K\to\mathbb R\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier and let \(K^*=\{s\in E^*:\langle s,x\rangle\geq0\ \forall x\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Class hierarchy on proper cones. The final self-scaled level is recorded only schematically because an exact supplied source for its defining scaling axiom was not located.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{sc}}(K)\) as all self-concordant barriers on \(K\). Define \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{lh}}(K)\subset\mathcal B_{\mathrm{sc}}(K)\) by the additional identity \(F(tx)=F(x)-\nu\ln t\) for every \(x\in\operatorname{int}K\) and \(t>0\). Define \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{ss}}(K)\subset\mathcal B_{\mathrm{lh}}(K)\) by requiring the standard primal--dual self-scaling axiom: the Hessian-induced scaling maps generated by interior points act as cone isomorphisms between \(K\) and \(K^*\), with the corresponding dual-barrier compatibility. Hence \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{ss}}(K)\subseteq\mathcal B_{\mathrm{lh}}(K)\subseteq\mathcal B_{\mathrm{sc}}(K)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: General self-concordant barriers satisfy the barrier differential inequalities. Logarithmically homogeneous barriers additionally transform by subtracting \(\nu\ln t\) under positive radial scaling. Self-scaled barriers form a still narrower conic class whose Hessian scalings are compatible with the primal and dual cones. These requirements give nested classes, not three synonymous names.

abla F(x),xangle=-
u\) and \(
abla^2F(x)x=-

Canonical barriers on direct products of Lorentz and positive-semidefinite cones inherit logarithmic homogeneity with additive parameter.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every assertion valid for all self-concordant barriers applies to the two narrower classes.
Primal--dual scaling conclusions require the self-scaled level and cannot be inferred from logarithmic homogeneity alone.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sum Rule for Self-Concordant Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded closure rule for sums of general self-concordant barriers; the common domain must be a valid barrier domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_i\) be a \(\nu_i\)-self-concordant barrier for \(i=1,2\), and suppose \(\operatorname{dom}F_1\cap\operatorname{dom}F_2\) is a nonempty barrier domain. Then
\[
F=F_1+F_2
\]
is a \((\nu_1+\nu_2)\)-self-concordant barrier on
\[
\operatorname{dom}F=\operatorname{dom}F_1\cap\operatorname{dom}F_2.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On their nonempty common domain, the sum of two self-concordant barriers is a self-concordant barrier whose parameter is the sum of the original parameters.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Logarithmic barrier for a self-concordant sublevel set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier construction for a nondegenerate sublevel set of a lower-bounded self-concordant function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be self-concordant with constant \(M_f\geq0\). Suppose \(\mathcal L( eta)=\{x\in\operatorname{dom}f:f(x)\leq eta\}\) has nonempty interior and \(f(x)\geq f^*\) for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\). For any \(

u\ln( eta-f(x))\), whose finite domain is \(\{x\in\operatorname{dom}f:f(x)< eta\}\), is a \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier for \(\mathcal L( eta)\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(x)=-\nu\ln(\beta-f(x))\text{ is a }\nu\text{-self-concordant barrier for }\mathcal L(\beta).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local-Distance Bound Under a Nonnegative Gradient Pairing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A global local-norm distance estimate obtained from a first-order orientation condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier. For every \(x,y\in\operatorname{dom}F\), if
\[

then
\[
\|y-x\|_x\le \nu+2\sqrt{\nu}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nu-self-concordant barrier, if the displacement from x to y has nonnegative pairing with the gradient at x, then its local norm at x is at most nu plus twice the square root of nu.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gradient–Hessian definition of a self-concordant barrier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the barrier parameter and preserves the equivalent formulations for both singular and nonsingular Hessians.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a standard self-concordant function and \(
u>0\). It is a \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier for \(\operatorname{Dom}F\) if, for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}F\), \[\sup_{u\in\mathbb R^n}\left(2\langle F'(x),uangle-\langle F''(x)u,uangleight)\leq
u.\] Equivalently, for every \(u\in\mathbb R^n\), \[\langle F'(x),uangle^2\leq
u\langle F''(x)u,uangle,\qquad F''(x)\succeq
u^{-1}F'(x)F'(x)^T.\] If \(F''(x)\) is nonsingular, these are also equivalent to \[\left\langle [F''(x)]^{-1}F'(x),F'(x)ightangle\leq
u.\] The number \(
u\) is the barrier parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A standard self-concordant function is a nu-self-concordant barrier when its gradient is controlled by its Hessian with bound nu. The quadratic and matrix formulations remain valid for a singular Hessian; the inverse-Hessian formulation additionally requires nonsingularity.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is a standard self-concordant function}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is a }\nu\text{-self-concordant barrier exactly under the stated gradient--Hessian condition, with the stated singular- and nonsingular-Hessian formulations}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Concave Exponential Characterization of Self-Concordant Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded characterization using exponential transforms of a barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier with \(\nu>0\), and define
\[
\xi_p(x)=\exp\{-F(x)/p\}.
\]
Then, for every \(p\ge\nu\), \(\xi_p\) is concave on \(\operatorname{dom}F\). Conversely, if \(\xi_\nu\) is concave on \(\operatorname{dom}F\), then \(F\) satisfies the self-concordant-barrier condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every exponential transform exp(-F/p) with p at least the barrier parameter is concave on the barrier domain. Conversely, concavity at the parameter value characterizes the barrier condition.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is a }\nu\text{-self-concordant barrier for the forward implication}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recession-Direction Inequality for a Self-Concordant Barrier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A gradient–Hessian inequality along recession directions of a general barrier domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier, and let \(h\in\mathbb E\) satisfy \(x+\tau h\in\operatorname{dom}F\) for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}F\) and every \(\tau\ge 0\). Then, for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}F\),
\[
\bigl\langle \nabla^2F(x)h,h\bigr\rangle^{1/2}\le \bigl\langle-\nabla F(x),h\bigr\rangle.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a self-concordant barrier, the local Hessian norm of any recession direction is at most the negative gradient pairing with that direction, at every point of the barrier domain.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Self-Scaled Barrier on a Proper Cone
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\subset E\) be a proper cone, let \(K^*\subset E^*\) be its dual, and let \(F:\operatorname{int}K\to\mathbb R\) be a logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier. Denote \(H_x=\nabla^2F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional primal--dual cone setting. This candidate states the characteristic scaling structure but requires an exact source for the conventional normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A self-scaled barrier is a logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier for which the Hessian scaling is compatible with the cone and its dual: for every \(x\in\operatorname{int}K\), \(H_x\) is a linear isomorphism satisfying \(H_x(\operatorname{int}K)=\operatorname{int}K^*\), and the barrier obeys the standard self-scaling identity relating \(F\), its dual barrier \(F_*\), and the transformation induced by \(H_x\). Equivalently in the symmetric-cone model, every pair of interior primal points admits a cone automorphism under which the canonical barrier changes only by an additive constant, and the associated inverse action scales dual variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A self-scaled barrier is not merely logarithmically homogeneous. Its Hessian provides primal-to-dual cone isomorphisms, and these isomorphisms are compatible with the barrier and its Fenchel-dual barrier. On symmetric cones this yields automorphisms that can move any interior point to any other while changing the canonical barrier only by a constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining extra structure is the cone-isomorphism and dual-compatibility property of \(H_x\), beyond self-concordance and logarithmic homogeneity.
special_cases_latex: On \(\mathbb R_+^n\), \(F(x)=-\sum_i\ln x_i\) is the canonical self-scaled barrier.
On \(\mathbb S_+^n\), \(F(X)=-\ln\det X\) supplies the canonical primal--dual matrix scaling.
On a Lorentz cone, \(F(z,t)=-\ln(t^2-\|z\|_2^2)\) supplies the canonical Lorentz scaling.
immediate_consequences_latex: The cone must admit the corresponding homogeneous primal--dual scaling structure.
Direct products of canonical symmetric-cone barriers retain blockwise scaling structure.
boundary_notes: No inspected supplied source states the full conventional self-scaled-barrier definition with its normalization.
The transitivity of a cone automorphism group alone is insufficient; barrier compatibility is also required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closure Calculus for Self-Concordant Barriers
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For each \(i\), let \(F_i\) be a \(\nu_i\)-self-concordant barrier on an open convex domain \(D_i\) in a finite-dimensional space. Barrier parameters refer to the standard normalization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A definition of the standard construction calculus as a collection of parameter-tracked closure operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The barrier construction calculus consists of the following parameter-tracked operations: (i) affine pullback, \(F\mapsto F\circ(A\cdot+b)\), on \(\{x:Ax+b\in D\}\), preserving parameter \(
u\); (ii) addition on a common space, \(F_1+F_2\), producing a barrier on \(D_1\cap D_2\) with parameter \(
u_1+
u_2\); (iii) direct products, \((x_1,\ldots,x_m)\mapsto\sum_iF_i(x_i)\), with domain \(\prod_iD_i\) and parameter \(\sum_i
u_i\); and (iv) supported epigraph or compatible-composition lifts, with the parameter prescribed by the corresponding construction theorem. A valid construction must have nonempty open domain and must preserve boundary blow-up for the represented set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Barrier construction calculus means the closure rules that build new barriers from known ones while tracking domains and parameters. Affine inverse images preserve the parameter, sums construct barriers for intersections, separable sums construct barriers for Cartesian products, and specific epigraph or compatible nonlinear lifts have their own stated parameter updates. Domain nonemptiness and boundary behavior remain part of every construction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
The elementary affine, intersection, and product rules transform certified barriers into certified barriers with parameters \(
u\), \(
u_1+
u_2\), and \(\sum_i
u_i\), respectively.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The direct-product rule is the intersection rule after lifting each \(F_i\) to the product space by its coordinate projection.
special_cases_latex: Restricting a barrier to an affine slice is an affine pullback.
The logarithmic barrier for finitely many scalar inequalities is the sum of their scalar logarithmic barriers.
immediate_consequences_latex: Barrier parameters accumulate additively under independent constraint-family assembly.
Redundant represented constraints may enlarge the constructed parameter even when the underlying convex set is unchanged.
boundary_notes: Arbitrary nonlinear composition does not preserve self-concordance; compatibility hypotheses are essential.
Projection or partial minimization requires a separate implicit-barrier theorem and is not an automatic elementary rule.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to product directions belonging to the recession cone of the barrier domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K\subset\mathbb E_2 be a cone, set K_0:=K\times\{0\}\subset\mathbb E_2\times\mathbb E_3, let Q_2\subset\mathbb E_2\times\mathbb E_3 be convex, and let \Phi be a barrier for Q_2. knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every direction (s,0) with s in K is a recession direction of the barrier domain, the barrier gradient has nonpositive inner product with each such direction at every interior point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cone-compatible composition rule for self-concordant barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General construction theorem for a self-concordant barrier on a projected lifted set defined by a cone-concave, barrier-compatible mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\xi:E_1\to E_2\) be concave with respect to a convex cone \(K\subset E_2\), let \(Q\subseteq\operatorname{dom}\xi\), and let \(F\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier for \(Q\) with which \(\xi\) is \(\beta\)-compatible. Let \(\Phi\) be a \(\mu\)-self-concordant barrier for a closed convex set \(Q_2\subset E_2\times E_3\), and suppose
\[
K\times\{0\}\subseteq\operatorname{rec}(Q_2).
\]
Then
\[
\Psi(x,z)=\Phi(\xi(x),z)+\beta^3F(x)
\]
is a self-concordant barrier, with parameter \(\widehat\nu=\mu+\beta^3\nu\), for
\[
\widehat Q=\left\{(x,z)\in Q\times E_3:\exists y\in E_2,\ \xi(x)\geq_K y,\ (y,z)\in Q_2\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If xi is cone-concave and beta-compatible with a parameter-nu self-concordant barrier on Q, Phi is a parameter-mu self-concordant barrier on the closed convex set Q2, and every direction in K times zero is a recession direction of Q2, then Phi composed with xi plus beta cubed times F is a self-concordant barrier on the stated projected lifted set. Its parameter is mu plus beta cubed times nu.
assumptions_latex: \xi:E_1\to E_2\text{ is concave with respect to the convex cone }K\subset E_2.
\Phi\text{ is a }\mu\text{-self-concordant barrier for a closed convex set }Q_2\subset E_2\times E_3.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Psi(x,z)=\Phi(\xi(x),z)+\beta^3F(x)\text{ is a self-concordant barrier for }\widehat Q\text{ with parameter }\widehat\nu=\mu+\beta^3\nu.

With the notation and ambient hypotheses of the preceding barrier construction, the second directional derivative of \(\Psi\) satisfies
\[
D_2=\Delta_2+\beta^3\sigma_3

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A smooth second-order chain-rule identity separating outer-barrier curvature from curvature of the inner mapping; it is not a nonsmooth second-directional-derivative result.

abla^2\Phi(\xi(x),z)l,langle+\langle

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine Pullback and Restriction of a Barrier
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:D\to\mathbb R\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on an open convex set \(D\subset E_1\). Let \(\mathcal A:E_0\to E_1\) be affine, \(\mathcal A(x)=Ax+b\), and assume \(D_0=\mathcal A^{-1}(D)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional affine inverse images, including parametrized affine slices. The pullback Hessian may be degenerate if \(A\) is not injective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The affine pullback barrier is \(\Phi:D_0\to\mathbb R\), \(\Phi(x)=F(Ax+b)\). It is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier for the represented domain \(D_0=\{x:Ax+b\in D\}\), with \[D^k\Phi(x)[h_1,\ldots,h_k]=D^kF(Ax+b)[Ah_1,\ldots,Ah_k],\qquad k=1,2,3.\] If an affine slice \(D\cap(a+V)\) is parametrized by \(x=a+Bu\), its restricted barrier is \(u\mapsto F(a+Bu)\) on \(\{u:a+Bu\in D\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composing a self-concordant barrier with an affine map gives a barrier on the affine inverse image of its domain and preserves the barrier parameter. Restriction to an affine slice is the same operation after parametrizing the slice. Directional derivatives are obtained by applying the linear part of the affine map to every direction argument.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi=F\circ\mathcal A\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(\mathcal A^{-1}(D)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Affine restriction is pullback under the embedding \(u\mapsto a+Bu\).
For an invertible affine coordinate change, pullback and pushforward give equivalent barrier models with the same parameter.
special_cases_latex: For \(D=\mathbb R_{++}^m\) and \(\mathcal A(x)=b-Ax\), the pullback is \(-\sum_i\ln(b_i-a_i^Tx)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The local Hessian is \(\nabla^2\Phi(x)=A^*\nabla^2F(Ax+b)A\).
Directions in \(\ker A\) are invisible to the pullback and lie in the Hessian kernel.
boundary_notes: If the affine inverse image is empty, no barrier domain is obtained.
For a barrier on the closure of the represented set, affine degeneracy may require relative-interior or quotient interpretation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Product and Intersection Assembly of Barriers
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F_i:D_i\to\mathbb R\) be \(\nu_i\)-self-concordant barriers, \(i=1,\ldots,m\). For intersections assume \(D_i\subset E\) and \(D=\bigcap_iD_i\neq\varnothing\). For products allow \(D_i\subset E_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite products and finite intersections under the standard self-concordance normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The intersection barrier is \[F_{\cap}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i(x),\qquad x\in igcap_{i=1}^mD_i,\] and has parameter \(
u_{\cap}=\sum_i
u_i\). The product barrier is \[F_{	imes}(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i(x_i),\qquad (x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in\prod_{i=1}^mD_i,\] and has parameter \(
u_{	imes}=\sum_i
u_i\). More generally, for affine representations \(\mathcal A_i:E_0	o E_i\), \(\sum_iF_i(\mathcal A_i x)\) is a barrier with parameter \(\sum_i
u_i\) on \(\{x:\mathcal A_i x\in D_i\  orall i\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add the component barriers to represent either a common-space intersection or a Cartesian product. In both cases the domain is the corresponding intersection or product, and the certified barrier parameters add. Combining affine pullbacks gives the same rule for multiple represented constraint families.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_{\cap}\) and \(F_{\times}\) are self-concordant barriers with parameter \(\sum_{i=1}^m\nu_i\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The intersection rule is \(F_{\cap}=\sum_iF_i\circ\operatorname{id}_E\).
The product rule is \(F_{\times}=\sum_iF_i\circ P_i\), where \(P_i\) is the ith coordinate projection.
special_cases_latex: For scalar inequalities \(a_i^Tx<b_i\), summing \(-\ln(b_i-a_i^Tx)\) gives the polyhedral logarithmic barrier with parameter equal to the number of terms.
For direct products of Lorentz cones, the canonical barrier is the sum of the factor barriers and has twice the number of factors as parameter.
immediate_consequences_latex: The Hessian of a product barrier is block diagonal.
Repeated or redundant constraints remain separate terms and increase the certified additive parameter.
boundary_notes: The intersection must have nonempty interior in the working space, or a relative-interior reduction is required.
Parameter addition gives a valid certificate and need not be the least possible parameter for the resulting set.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Epigraph Lift of a Self-Concordant Barrier
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on an open convex domain \(D\subset E\). Define the closed epigraph \(\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t)\in D\times\mathbb R:t\geq f(x)\}\) and its open interior representation \(\mathcal E_f^\circ=\{(x,t):x\in D,\ t>f(x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact epigraph construction supported by the source. General perspective homogenization requires additional homogeneity hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The epigraph barrier associated with \(f\) is \[F_{\mathrm{epi}}(x,t)=f(x)-\ln\bigl(t-f(x)\bigr),\qquad (x,t)\in\mathcal E_f^\circ.\] It is a \((\nu+1)\)-self-concordant barrier for \(\operatorname{epi}f\). The slack coordinate \(s=t-f(x)>0\) contributes one scalar logarithmic-barrier unit. When a positively homogeneous perspective \(p(y,\tau)=\tau f(y/\tau)\) is introduced for \(\tau>0\), its epigraph is the conic homogenization \(\{(y,\tau,t):\tau>0,\ t>\tau f(y/\tau)\}\); a barrier transfer to that cone requires a separately verified perspective or affine-composition theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A self-concordant barrier \(f\) yields a barrier for its epigraph by adding the logarithmic barrier of the positive epigraph slack \(t-f(x)\). The resulting parameter is \(\nu+1\). The usual perspective lift homogenizes the epigraph, but its barrier status is not automatic without the additional hypotheses of an applicable perspective construction.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using the slack variable \(s=t-f(x)\), the barrier is \(f(x)-\ln s\) subject to \(s>0\) and \(t=f(x)+s\).
special_cases_latex: For \(f(x)=-\ln x\) on \(\mathbb R_{++}\), the construction gives \(-\ln x-\ln(t+\ln x)\) on \(t>-\ln x\).
immediate_consequences_latex: An objective epigraph can be incorporated into a barrier model with one additional certified parameter unit.
Affine transformations of \((x,t)\) can be combined with this construction by affine pullback.
boundary_notes: The construction requires that \(f\) itself be a self-concordant barrier, not merely an arbitrary convex function.
The source-supported epigraph formula should not be conflated with an unrestricted perspective closure rule.

source_refs.locator: Theorem 5.3.5, epigraph formula and parameter \(\nu+1\)

review_flags: The epigraph claim is directly supported; the perspective paragraph is deliberately limited because no exact supplied perspective-barrier theorem was located.
knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph Lift of a Self-Concordant Barrier

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit self-concordant barrier construction for the epigraph of the exponential function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Q_2:=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^2:t\ge e^x\}, with \operatorname{int}(Q_2)=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^2:t>0,\ \ln t>x\}. Define F_2:\operatorname{int}(Q_2)\to\mathbb{R} by F_2(x,t):=-\ln t-\ln(\ln t-x). Then F_2 is a 3\text{-self-concordant barrier for }Q_2.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit self-concordant barrier construction for the epigraph of the extended scalar entropy function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }Q_3:=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^2:x\ge 0,\ t\ge x\ln x\},\quad 0\ln 0:=0.\ \text{Define }F_3:\operatorname{int}(Q_3)\to\mathbb{R}\text{ by }F_3(x,t):=-\ln x-\ln\bigl(t-x\ln x\bigr),\quad \operatorname{int}(Q_3)=\{(x,t):x>0,\ t>x\ln x\}.\ \text{Then }F_3\text{ is a }3\text{-self-concordant barrier for }Q_3.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Let Q3 be the epigraph of x log x on the nonnegative half-line, with 0 log 0 defined as 0. On its interior, where x is positive and t is strictly greater than x log x, the function F3(x,t) = -log x - log(t - x log x) is a 3-self-concordant barrier for Q3.

children.title: Epigraph–Perspective Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural relationship between epigraph lifts and their homogeneous perspective forms.

notation.meaning: Closed perspective of the convex function

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-perspective convention including the zero-scale recession face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the closed perspective by \[\bar f(x,s)=\begin{cases}s f(x/s),&s>0,\\ f^{\infty}(x),&s=0,\\ +\infty,&s<0.\end{cases}\] Then \(\bar f\) is proper, closed, convex, and positively homogeneous, and its epigraph satisfies \[\operatorname{epi}\bar f=\overline{\operatorname{cone}}\bigl(\{(x,1,t):(x,t)\in\operatorname{epi}f\}\bigr).\] Conversely, the unit-scale section recovers the original epigraph: \((x,t)\in\operatorname{epi}f\) if and only if \((x,1,t)\in\operatorname{epi}\bar f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective epigraph is the closed conic hull of the unit-scale epigraph, whose scale-one slice recovers the original epigraph.
knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph–Perspective Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is plausible and fits the correspondence leaf, but no citation is supplied. The exact closed-perspective convention, recession-face formula, and closed-conic-hull identity require an authoritative section, theorem, or proposition locator before review can determine reliability.

children.title: Lifted-Domain Boundary Regimes
children.top_down_role: Boundary behavior specific to auxiliary variables introduced by nonlinear lifting.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex, with closed perspective \(\bar f\).
A lifted barrier is defined on the interior region with positive scale \(s>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The zero-scale face is governed by \(f^{\infty}\), while interior barrier blow-up occurs as scale or defining slack vanishes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary decomposition for closed perspective lifts and their positive-scale barriers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the closed perspective, points with \(s>0\) satisfy \(\bar f(x,s)=sf(x/s)\), whereas the zero-scale face satisfies \(\bar f(x,0)=f^{\infty}(x)\). Thus finite points at \(s=0\) encode recession directions rather than ordinary evaluations of \(f\). A barrier constructed only on the positive-scale interior must diverge along finite interior sequences approaching \(s=0\) or any active lifted-domain boundary. If the recession face is omitted instead of closed by \(f^{\infty}\), the resulting perspective epigraph need not be closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At positive scale the lift evaluates the perspective; at zero scale it records recession behavior, and omitting that face can destroy closedness.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Domain Boundary Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the record has no source. The claims about the zero-scale recession face, barrier divergence at that face, and failure of closedness when it is omitted require an authoritative locator and convention check.

children.title: Polarity-Conjugacy Barrier Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Barrier transfer through polar and dual representations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fenchel-Conjugate Transfer of Self-Concordant Geometry
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be a closed, strictly convex self-concordant function on an open convex set \(D\subset E\), with \(\nabla^2f(x)\succ0\). Define \(f_*:E^*\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) by Fenchel conjugacy.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Legendre-type, finite-dimensional nondegenerate regime. The statement concerns conjugate self-concordance; identification with a polar cone needs conic homogeneity and sign conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The conjugate is \[f_*(s)=\sup_{x\in D}\{\langle s,xangle-f(x)\}.\] Its open domain is \(D_* = 
abla f(D)\). For \(s=
abla f(x)\), \[
abla f_*(s)=x,\qquad 
abla^2f_*(s)=[
abla^2f(x)]^{-1}.\] Moreover, \(f_*\) is self-concordant with the same self-concordance constant as \(f\). If \(f\) is a logarithmically homogeneous barrier on a proper cone, the gradient map, after the conventional sign choice, identifies the primal interior with the interior of the dual or polar cone, and the conjugate provides the corresponding dual barrier geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fenchel conjugacy transfers a nondegenerate self-concordant function to the dual space. The gradient maps the primal domain onto the conjugate domain, the conjugate gradient is its inverse, and the two Hessians are inverse at paired points. In a logarithmically homogeneous conic setting, this becomes the barrier correspondence between a cone and its dual or polar representation, subject to the chosen sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
For \(s=
abla f(x)\), \(
abla f_*(s)=x\), \(
abla^2f_*(s)=[
abla^2f(x)]^{-1}\), and \(f_*\) is self-concordant with the same constant.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The maps \(\nabla f:D\to D_*\) and \(\nabla f_*:D_*\to D\) are mutual inverses.
At paired points, the primal and dual local norms satisfy \(\|h\|_x=\|\nabla^2f(x)h\|_s^*\).
special_cases_latex: For \(f(x)=-\sum_i\ln x_i\) on \(\mathbb R_{++}^n\), the conjugate domain is \(\mathbb R_{--}^n\); applying the sign map gives the usual positive dual cone.
immediate_consequences_latex: Primal Hessian conditioning is reciprocally represented by the dual Hessian at a conjugate point.
Dual barrier statements must track whether the dual cone is defined using nonnegative or nonpositive pairings.
boundary_notes: Fenchel conjugacy alone does not identify the conjugate domain with a polar cone for an arbitrary nonconic domain.
The displayed inverse-Hessian relation requires nondegeneracy and the Legendre-type domain assumptions.

source_refs.locator: Equation (5.1.30), Lemma 5.1.6, equations (5.1.31)--(5.1.34), and Theorem 5.1.17

review_flags: The conjugacy statement is directly supported; the polar-cone specialization is qualified because it additionally depends on conic homogeneity and sign conventions.

children.title: Polar-Domain Barrier Constructions
children.top_down_role: Transfer of barrier structure between a convex domain and its polar representation.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a regular cone: closed, convex, pointed, and full-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_{K^*}\) is a \(\nu\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier on \(\operatorname{int}K^*\).

notation.meaning: Barrier induced on the dual polar domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cone polarity version; the sign convention places the conjugate on the positive dual cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K^*:=\{s\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle s,x\rangle\ge0\text{ for every }x\in K\}\). Define
\[
F_{K^*}(s):=F^*(-s)=\sup_{x\in\operatorname{int}K}\{-\langle s,x\rangle-F(x)\}.
\]
Then \(\operatorname{dom}F_{K^*}=\operatorname{int}K^*\), and \(F_{K^*}\) is a \(\nu\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier there. An additive normalization constant in \(F\) changes only the additive constant in \(F_{K^*}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conjugating a logarithmically homogeneous barrier with the appropriate sign constructs a barrier having the same parameter on the polar dual cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Polar-Domain Barrier Constructions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The signed-conjugacy formula and preservation of the logarithmic-homogeneity parameter are plausible and fit the representation container, but no inspectable source is supplied for the exact domain and barrier theorem.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^*\) is self-concordant on \(\nabla F(D)\), with inverse Hessian transported by conjugacy.

notation.meaning: Gradient image of the primal domain

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(F^*(y):=\sup_{x\in D}\{\langle y,xangle-F(x)\}\) and \(D^*:=
abla F(D)\). Then \(F^*\) is self-concordant on \(D^*\). For \(y=
abla F(x)\), conjugacy gives
\[

abla F^*(y)=x,\qquad 
abla^2F^*(y)= igl(
abla^2F(x) igr)^{-1}.
\]
If \(F\) is a barrier and the gradient image is the interior of the intended dual domain, then \(F^*\) is a barrier on that domain.

children.title: Polarity Qualification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Domain features that require closure, pointedness, or dimensional reduction before polar transfer.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a convex cone and \(K^*:=\{s\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle s,x\rangle\ge 0\text{ for every }x\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Full-dimensionality of \(K\) and pointedness of \(K\) are necessary for both \(K\) and \(K^*\) to have nonempty Euclidean interiors.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric qualification boundary for full-space polar barrier formulas; it does not claim that closedness follows from the displayed arguments.

source_refs.locator: 6.3 Polar and Dual Cones p. 122
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\operatorname{span}K\ne\mathbb{R}^n\), then \(K\) has empty Euclidean interior. If \(\operatorname{lin}K\ne\{0\}\), then \(K^*\subseteq(\operatorname{lin}K)^\perp\), so \(K^*\) has empty Euclidean interior. Consequently, full-dimensional barriers on both primal and dual cones require \(K\) to be full-dimensional and pointed. Degenerate cases must instead be treated in an appropriate span or quotient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a cone is not full-dimensional, its own Euclidean interior is empty; if it is not pointed, its dual cone has empty Euclidean interior. Full-space primal-dual barriers therefore require full-dimensionality and pointedness.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Canonical Logarithmic Barrier Families
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Canonical barriers are attached to explicit standard representations of open convex sets or proper cones. All parameters below use the standard self-concordance normalization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional polyhedral, Lorentz-cone, and positive-semidefinite families, together with their finite products and affine pullbacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The canonical families include: \[F_{\mathrm{orth}}(x)=-\sum_{i=1}^m\ln x_i\quad(x\in\mathbb R_{++}^m),\qquad 
u=m;\] \[F_{\mathrm{soc}}(z,t)=-\ln(t^2-\|z\|_2^2)\quad(t>\|z\|_2),\qquad 
u=2;\] \[F_{\mathrm{psd}}(X)=-\ln\det X\quad(X\in\mathbb S_{++}^n),\qquad 
u=n.\] Polyhedral barriers are affine pullbacks of \(F_{\mathrm{orth}}\); product-cone barriers are sums of factor barriers; semidefinite and Lorentz representations are likewise transported by affine pullback.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard reusable barrier families are the sum-of-logarithms barrier for the positive orthant, the logarithm of the Lorentz quadratic form for the second-order cone, and the log-determinant barrier for the positive-semidefinite cone. Their parameters are respectively the orthant dimension, two, and the matrix order. Products use sums and represented domains use affine pullbacks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed orthant, Lorentz, and positive-semidefinite functions are canonical self-concordant barriers with parameters \(m\), \(2\), and \(n\), respectively.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(P=\{x:b-Ax\in\mathbb R_+^m\}\), the polyhedral barrier is \(-\sum_{i=1}^m\ln(b_i-a_i^Tx)\).
For a direct product \(K=\prod_jK_j\), the canonical barrier is \(F_K=\sum_jF_{K_j}\) and \(\nu_K=\sum_j\nu_j\).
special_cases_latex: The scalar ray barrier \(-\ln x\) is both the one-dimensional orthant and one-dimensional semidefinite barrier.
A convex quadratic inequality with positive slack can often be represented by a scalar second-order-region barrier or by an affine Lorentz-cone lift.
immediate_consequences_latex: Linear, conic-quadratic, and semidefinite constraint blocks admit explicit barrier values, gradients, and Hessians.
The representation, not only the abstract feasible set, determines the immediately available canonical barrier.
boundary_notes: Nonsymmetric cones generally require different constructions and are not covered by these three formulas.
The additive parameter of a represented product need not be the smallest barrier parameter of the underlying set.

children.title: Polyhedral Logarithmic Barriers
children.top_down_role: Barriers induced by linear-inequality representations.

assumptions_latex: Every listed inequality is retained as part of the chosen representation.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter is representation-dependent and counts the displayed logarithmic terms, including redundant inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in P\), define
\[
F(x):=-\sum_{i=1}^m\log\bigl(b_i-a_i^Tx\bigr).
\]
Then \(F(x)\to+\infty\) whenever a sequence in \(P\) approaches a boundary point at which some represented slack vanishes. Moreover, \(F\) satisfies the self-concordance inequality and the barrier-gradient inequality with parameter \(m\); hence it is an \(m\)-self-concordant barrier for the open polyhedron \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summing negative logarithms of positive linear slacks gives a self-concordant polyhedral barrier whose parameter equals the number of represented inequalities.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative Direction on the Positive Orthant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines componentwise displacement relative to a strictly positive base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For x\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n and h\in\mathbb{R}^n, define, for i=1,\ldots,n, \delta_x^{(i)}(h):=\frac{h^{(i)}}{x^{(i)}},\qquad \delta_x(h):=\bigl(\delta_x^{(1)}(h),\ldots,\delta_x^{(n)}(h)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a strictly positive vector x and any direction h, the relative direction delta_x(h) has coordinates h_i divided by x_i.

children.top_down_role: Canonical barriers for convex quadratic and Lorentz-cone representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Barrier Representations for Convex Quadratic and Lorentz Constraints
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q(x)=\alpha+\langle a,x\rangle+\tfrac12\langle Ax,x\rangle\) with \(A\succeq0\), and let \(\beta\in\mathbb R\). Let \(A=B^*B\). The Lorentz cone is \(\mathcal L^{r+1}=\{(z,t):t\geq\|z\|_2\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex quadratic sublevel and second-order-cone representations with strictly positive slack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The strict quadratic sublevel domain is \(D_q=\{x:\beta-q(x)>0\}\). Its scalar logarithmic barrier is \[F_q(x)=-\ln(\beta-q(x)),\qquad x\in D_q,\] and is a \(1\)-self-concordant barrier for the corresponding second-order region. A norm inequality \(\|Bx+c\|_2<d^Tx+e\) is the affine inverse image of \(\operatorname{int}\mathcal L^{r+1}\) and therefore has barrier \[F_{\mathcal L}(x)=-\ln\bigl((d^Tx+e)^2-\|Bx+c\|_2^2\bigr),\] with parameter \(2\). Finite families are assembled by summing these barriers, so their certified parameters add.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex quadratic inequality with positive concave slack can use the negative logarithm of that slack as a one-parameter barrier. A second-order-cone inequality is represented by an affine Lorentz-cone map and uses the negative logarithm of the Lorentz quadratic form, with parameter two. Multiple quadratic or cone constraints are combined by summing their barriers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_q\) is a \(1\)-self-concordant barrier on \(D_q\), and \(F_{\mathcal L}\) is a \(2\)-self-concordant barrier on \(\{x:\|Bx+c\|_2<d^Tx+e\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The Lorentz representation is \((Bx+c,d^Tx+e)\in\operatorname{int}\mathcal L^{r+1}\).
Completing the square or factoring \(A=B^*B\) converts many convex quadratic sublevel constraints into rotated or ordinary second-order-cone representations after introducing auxiliary variables.
special_cases_latex: For \(q(x)=\|x\|_2^2\) and \(\beta=1\), \(-\ln(1-\|x\|_2^2)\) is the unit-ball barrier.
For \(B=I\), \(c=0\), and scalar \(t\), the Lorentz barrier is \(-\ln(t^2-\|x\|_2^2)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Affine substitutions preserve the stated parameters.
A quadratically constrained convex program obtains an explicit barrier by summing one term per scalar quadratic slack or per chosen cone block.
boundary_notes: The scalar quadratic-slack formula requires the slack to be concave, equivalently the quadratic function in the sublevel constraint to be convex.
Different cone lifts of the same quadratic set can have different additive parameter certificates.

children.title: Convex Quadratic Barriers
children.top_down_role: Canonical barriers associated with convex regions represented by quadratic inequalities.

assumptions_latex: \(D:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:c^Tx+d>\|Ax+b\|_2\}\) is nonempty, and \(Ah=0\) together with \(c^Th=0\) implies \(h=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The function \(F(x):=-\log(-q(x))\) is the injective affine pullback of the Lorentz-cone logarithmic barrier and is a self-concordant barrier on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex quadratic barriers obtained from an injective affine section of the Lorentz cone, with an explicit positive-sheet condition.

source_refs.locator: 3.5.2 Conic quadratic representations p. 132

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T(x):=(c^Tx+d,Ax+b)\). For \(x\in D\), one has \(-q(x)=(c^Tx+d)^2-\|Ax+b\|_2^2>0\), and therefore \[F(x):=-\log(-q(x))=-\log\bigl((c^Tx+d)^2-\|Ax+b\|_2^2\bigr).\] Thus \(F\) is the affine pullback through \(T\) of the Lorentz-cone logarithmic barrier. The injectivity assumption on the linear part of \(T\) makes the pullback Hessian positive definite, and \(F\) is a self-concordant barrier on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex quadratic written as a Lorentz difference of squares has a negative-log barrier obtained by an injective affine pullback of the Lorentz-cone barrier.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Quadratic Barriers

children.title: Second-Order Cone Barriers
children.top_down_role: Canonical barriers for Lorentz-cone domains.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(t,u)=-\log(t^2-\|u\|_2^2)\) is a \(2\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier on \(L_{r+1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard Lorentz-cone barrier with parameter two, independent of cone dimension.

source_refs.locator: 3.5.2 Conic quadratic representations p. 132

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
F(t,u):=-\log\bigl(t^2-\|u\|_2^2\bigr),\qquad (t,u)\in L_{r+1}.
\]
Then \(F\) is a self-concordant barrier and satisfies
\[
F(\lambda t,\lambda u)=F(t,u)-2\log\lambda\qquad(\lambda>0).
\]
Thus \(F\) is \(2\)-logarithmically homogeneous and has barrier parameter \(2\). It diverges to \(+\infty\) as \(t^2-\|u\|_2^2\downarrow0\) within the cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The negative logarithm of the Lorentz quadratic determinant is a parameter-two logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier.
knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Cone Barriers

children.title: Quadratic-to-Cone Representations
children.top_down_role: Lifted or transformed representations connecting convex quadratic regions to second-order cones.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conditions \(q(x)\le0\) and \(c^Tx+d\ge0\) are equivalent to one affine second-order-cone constraint.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[q(x)\le0\ \text{ and }\ c^Tx+d\ge0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \|Ax+b\|_2\le c^Tx+d \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad T(x)\in\mathcal{Q}_{r+1}.\] Likewise, \(q(x)<0\) and \(c^Tx+d>0\) are equivalent to \(T(x)\in\operatorname{int}\mathcal{Q}_{r+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A difference-of-squares quadratic inequality with its positive-sheet condition is exactly one affine Lorentz-cone constraint.

children.title: Degenerate Quadratic Regimes
children.top_down_role: Quadratic representations requiring reduction because of singularity or missing interior.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Empty strict feasibility, omission of a sheet condition, or a noninjective affine Lorentz map prevents the intended full-dimensional quadratic-barrier interpretation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundaries caused by empty interior, an unselected quadratic sheet, or flat directions in the affine Lorentz representation.

source_refs.locator: 3.5.2 Conic quadratic representations p. 132

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(D=\varnothing\), no ordinary barrier exists on the represented strict positive-sheet region. If \(q(x)<0\) is imposed without selecting the sign of \(c^Tx+d\), the positive and negative Lorentz sheets are combined; although each sheet is convex after the appropriate sign convention, their union is generally nonconvex. Finally, if a nonzero \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies \(Ah=0\) and \(c^Th=0\), then \(T(x+\tau h)=T(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\tau\in\mathbb{R}\), so the pullback Hessian is singular along \(h\). A positive-definite local barrier metric then requires reduction by the flat directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic cone barrier requires a nonempty strict sheet, an explicit sheet choice, and removal of any directions on which the affine Lorentz representation is constant.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Quadratic Regimes

children.title: Semidefinite Log-Determinant Barriers
children.top_down_role: Spectral barriers on positive-definite matrix cones.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\) denotes the cone of real symmetric positive-definite matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(X)=-\log\det X\) is an \(n\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier on \(\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\).

notation.meaning: Trace inner product on symmetric matrices

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real symmetric positive-definite cone with the trace inner product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(X\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\), define \(F(X):=-\log\det X\). Its first two derivatives are
\[
DF(X)[H]=-\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}H),\qquad D^2F(X)[H,H]=\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}HX^{-1}H).
\]
The function \(F\) is self-concordant, tends to \(+\infty\) when a positive eigenvalue approaches zero, and satisfies
\[
F(\lambda X)=F(X)-n\log\lambda\qquad(\lambda>0).
\]
Hence it is an \(n\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative log-determinant is the canonical parameter-n self-concordant barrier on the positive-definite matrix cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Log-Determinant Barriers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The log-determinant theorem and theorem content kind are mathematically standard and internally consistent, but the record supplies no citation with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function $F:\operatorname{int}(\mathbb{S}_+^n)\to\mathbb{R}$ defined by $F(X)=-\ln\det X$ is an $n$-self-concordant barrier for $\mathbb{S}_+^n$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The negative log-determinant on positive-definite symmetric matrices is an n-self-concordant barrier for the positive-semidefinite cone.

children.title: Nonsymmetric Cone Barriers
children.top_down_role: Barrier families for exponential, power, entropy, and related nonsymmetric cones.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed logarithmic expression is a self-concordant barrier on \(\operatorname{int}K_{\exp}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representative nonsymmetric-cone construction using the exponential cone; not an exhaustive family classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On
\[
\operatorname{int}K_{\exp}=\{(x,y,z):y>0,\ z>0,\ r(x,y,z)>0\},
\]
define
\[
F_{\exp}(x,y,z):=-\log y-\log z-\log r(x,y,z),
\qquad r(x,y,z):=\log(z/y)-x/y.
\]
This function is a self-concordant barrier for the exponential cone and diverges when \(y\downarrow0\), \(z\downarrow0\), or \(r(x,y,z)\downarrow0\). Analogous cone-specific constructions, rather than symmetry-based determinant formulas, are required for power, entropy, and related nonsymmetric cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exponential cone admits an explicit logarithmic self-concordant barrier, illustrating the cone-specific formulas needed for nonsymmetric cones.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsymmetric Cone Barriers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the displayed nonsymmetric-cone formula. The exact exponential-cone barrier is formula-sensitive, and the displayed expression may omit a logarithmic factor relative to standard logarithmically homogeneous constructions; an authoritative formula and parameter are required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonsymmetric cone barrier and the power-cone family
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let \(K\subset E\) be a closed, pointed, full-dimensional convex cone. A cone barrier is defined on \(\operatorname{int}K\); symmetry, homogeneity of the cone, and self-duality are not assumed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth barriers on regular cones, emphasizing barrier constructions that remain valid without symmetric-cone geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A nonsymmetric-cone barrier is a self-concordant barrier \(F:\operatorname{int}K\to\mathbb R\) whose definition and validity do not require \(K\) to be a homogeneous self-dual cone. A canonical family is obtained for \(0<\alpha<1\) on the power cone
\[
K_\alpha=\{(x_1,x_2,z)\in\mathbb R_+^2\times\mathbb R:x_1^\alpha x_2^{1-\alpha}\ge |z|\}.
\]
On its interior,
\[
\Psi_{P,\alpha}(x_1,x_2,z)=-\log\!\left(x_1^{2\alpha}x_2^{2(1-\alpha)}-z^2\right)-\log x_1-\log x_2
\]
is a \(4\)-self-concordant barrier. Thus this family supplies explicit local metrics \(\nabla^2\Psi_{P,\alpha}\) and barrier parameters without invoking a self-scaled or symmetric-cone structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsymmetric-cone barrier is a self-concordant barrier on the interior of a regular cone whose construction does not assume that the cone is homogeneous and self-dual. For the power cone \(K_\alpha\), with \(0<\alpha<1\), the displayed logarithmic function is defined exactly where \(x_1>0\), \(x_2>0\), and \(x_1^{2\alpha}x_2^{2(1-\alpha)}>z^2\); it is a self-concordant barrier with parameter \(4\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Psi_{P,\alpha}\) is a \(4\)-self-concordant barrier for \(K_\alpha\), furnishing an explicit barrier family that does not depend on symmetric-cone scaling.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\operatorname{int}K_\alpha=\{(x_1,x_2,z):x_1>0,\ x_2>0,\ x_1^\alpha x_2^{1-\alpha}>|z|\}\).
special_cases_latex: For the one-sided power cone \(K_\alpha^+=\{(x_1,x_2,z):x_1,x_2\ge0,\ x_1^\alpha x_2^{1-\alpha}\ge z\}\), the source gives the \(3\)-self-concordant barrier \(-\log(x_1^\alpha x_2^{1-\alpha}-z)-\log x_1-\log x_2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The barrier diverges when \(x_1\downarrow0\), \(x_2\downarrow0\), or \(x_1^\alpha x_2^{1-\alpha}\downarrow |z|\).
The parameter \(4\) controls the local-gradient inequality \(\|\nabla\Psi_{P,\alpha}(x)\|_{x,*}^2\le4\).
boundary_notes: The term “nonsymmetric” concerns the absence of a homogeneous self-dual cone structure; it does not mean that the Hessian is nonsymmetric.
Exponential- and entropy-cone barriers are nearby families but are not asserted by this record.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A 4-self-concordant barrier for the power cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit barrier for the source-referenced power cone; the defining formula for that cone is not reproduced because its referenced definition is outside this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and let \(K_\alpha\) be the power cone specified by the referenced definition. Suppose \(\Phi(y,z)=-\ln(y^2-z^2)\) has parameter \(\mu=2\), \(F(x)=-\ln x^{(1)}-\ln x^{(2)}\) has parameter \(\nu=2\), and \(\xi(x)=(x^{(1)})^\alpha(x^{(2)})^{1-\alpha}\) is \(1\)-compatible with \(F\). Then \(\Psi_P(x,z)=-\ln((x^{(1)})^{2\alpha}(x^{(2)})^{2(1-\alpha)}-z^2)-\ln x^{(1)}-\ln x^{(2)}\) is a \(4\)-self-concordant barrier for \(K_\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the power cone referenced by the source, combining the parameter-two quadratic barrier, the parameter-two orthant barrier, and the 1-compatible weighted geometric mean gives the displayed self-concordant barrier with parameter four.
assumptions_latex: K_\alpha\text{ is the power cone specified by the source-referenced definition}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Psi_P(x,z)=-\ln\!\left((x^{(1)})^{2\alpha}(x^{(2)})^{2(1-\alpha)}-z^2\right)-\ln x^{(1)}-\ln x^{(2)}\text{ is a }4\text{-self-concordant barrier for }K_\alpha.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), \(x\in\operatorname{int}\mathbb R_+^2\), \(h\in\mathbb R^2\), \(\xi(x)=(x^{(1)})^\alpha(x^{(2)})^{1-\alpha}\), and \(\delta_i=h^{(i)}/x^{(i)}\) for \(i=1,2\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the positive orthant, the first three repeated directional derivatives of the weighted geometric mean have the displayed scaled-coordinate formulas.

children.title: Hyperbolic-Polynomial Barriers
children.top_down_role: Barriers induced by hyperbolicity-cone geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(p\) is a homogeneous polynomial of degree \(d\ge1\), hyperbolic with respect to \(e\).
\(\Lambda_{++}(p,e)\) is the connected component of \(\{x:p(x)>0\}\) containing \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x)=-\log p(x)\) is a \(d\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier on \(\Lambda_{++}(p,e)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Guler-type barrier theorem for homogeneous hyperbolic polynomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
F(x):=-\log p(x),\qquad x\in\Lambda_{++}(p,e).
\]
Then \(F\) is a self-concordant barrier for the open hyperbolicity cone. Homogeneity of \(p\) gives
\[
F(\lambda x)=F(x)-d\log\lambda\qquad(\lambda>0),
\]
so the barrier is \(d\)-logarithmically homogeneous and has parameter \(d\). Moreover, \(F(x_k)\to+\infty\) whenever \(x_k\) approaches a finite boundary point of the cone with \(p(x_k)\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The negative logarithm of a degree-d hyperbolic polynomial is a parameter-d logarithmically homogeneous barrier on its hyperbolicity cone.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Barrier induced by a hyperbolic polynomial
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space. Let \(p:E\to\mathbb R\) be a nonzero homogeneous polynomial of degree \(d\), and fix \(e\in E\) with \(p(e)>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional homogeneous hyperbolic polynomials and the open hyperbolicity cone containing the distinguished direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The polynomial \(p\) is hyperbolic with respect to \(e\) when, for every \(x\in E\), the univariate polynomial \(t\mapsto p(x-te)\) has only real roots. Its open hyperbolicity cone is
\[
\Lambda_{++}(p,e)=\text{the connected component of }\{x\in E:p(x)>0\}\text{ containing }e,
\]
and \(\Lambda_+(p,e)=\operatorname{cl}\Lambda_{++}(p,e)\). The hyperbolic-polynomial barrier is
\[
F_p(x)=-\log p(x),\qquad x\in\Lambda_{++}(p,e).
\]
It is logarithmically homogeneous of degree \(d\), since \(F_p(\tau x)=F_p(x)-d\log\tau\) for every \(\tau>0\). The canonical barrier theorem asserts that \(F_p\) is a \(d\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier for \(\Lambda_+(p,e)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A homogeneous polynomial \(p\) is hyperbolic in direction \(e\) if every line parallel to \(e\) produces a real-rooted univariate polynomial. The component of \(p>0\) containing \(e\) is its open hyperbolicity cone. The associated barrier is \(-\log p\) on that component; homogeneity gives logarithmic degree \(d\), and the standard barrier result assigns parameter \(d\).
assumptions_latex: For every \(x\in E\), all roots of \(t\mapsto p(x-te)\) are real.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_p=-\log p\) is the canonical degree-\(d\) logarithmically homogeneous barrier on \(\Lambda_{++}(p,e)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(\lambda_1(x),\ldots,\lambda_d(x)\) are defined by \(p(x-te)=p(e)\prod_{i=1}^d(\lambda_i(x)-t)\), then \(\Lambda_{++}(p,e)=\{x:\lambda_i(x)>0\ \forall i\}\).
special_cases_latex: For \(p(X)=\det X\) on symmetric matrices and \(e=I\), \(\Lambda_{++}(p,e)=\mathbb S_{++}^n\) and \(F_p(X)=-\log\det X\).
For \(p(x)=\prod_{i=1}^m a_i^Tx\), the barrier is \(-\sum_{i=1}^m\log(a_i^Tx)\) on the corresponding component.
immediate_consequences_latex: \(F_p(\tau x)=F_p(x)-d\log\tau\).
\(\langle\nabla F_p(x),x\rangle=-d\) wherever \(p(x)>0\).
boundary_notes: The real-rootedness condition is required in every direction \(x\), not merely near \(e\).
The inspected local source defines hyperbolicity but does not contain the exact self-concordant-barrier theorem; authoritative support for the parameter claim is still required.
review_flags: Needs an inspected authoritative source for the exact claim that \(-\log p\) is a degree-\(d\) self-concordant barrier on the hyperbolicity cone.
A local source was found for the definition of hyperbolicity, but partial support is insufficient for the complete slot.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polar-volume universal barrier
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\subset\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex with nonempty interior and no affine line. For \(x\in\operatorname{int}Q\), form the polar of \(Q-x\) at level one.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional general convex domains without explicit algebraic structure; the construction is primarily existential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\operatorname{int}Q\), define
\[
P_Q(x)=\{s\in\mathbb R^n:\langle s,z-x\rangle\le1\ \text{for every }z\in Q\},
\qquad V_Q(x)=\operatorname{vol}_n P_Q(x).
\]
The polar-volume universal barrier is
\[
U_Q(x)=c_1\log V_Q(x),\qquad x\in\operatorname{int}Q,
\]
where \(c_1>0\) is an absolute normalization constant. Universal-barrier theory states that absolute constants \(c_1,c_2>0\), independent of \(Q\) and \(n\), can be chosen so that \(U_Q\) is a \((c_2n)\)-self-concordant barrier for \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each interior point \(x\), translate the convex set by \(-x\), take its level-one polar, and measure the polar's \(n\)-dimensional volume. A fixed positive multiple of the logarithm of that volume is the universal barrier. Absolute constants make its self-concordance parameter proportional to the ambient dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There are absolute \(c_1,c_2>0\) for which \(U_Q(x)=c_1\log\operatorname{vol}_n P_Q(x)\) is a \((c_2n)\)-self-concordant barrier for \(Q\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(P_Q(x)=(Q-x)^\circ=\{s:\sigma_{Q-x}(s)\le1\}\), where \(\sigma\) is the support function.
special_cases_latex: When \(Q\) is bounded, every \(P_Q(x)\) contains the origin in its interior and has finite positive volume.
Affine changes of coordinates modify \(U_Q\) only by an additive constant determined by the determinant of the linear map.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every line-free finite-dimensional closed convex set with nonempty interior admits a dimension-controlled self-concordant barrier.
The resulting path-following iteration scale is governed by \(O(\sqrt n)\), apart from logarithmic accuracy factors.
boundary_notes: If \(Q\) contains a line, \(P_Q(x)\) is lower-dimensional and its \(n\)-volume vanishes, so this formulation is inapplicable.
The definition does not provide an efficient procedure for evaluating the volume or its derivatives.

notation.meaning: Polar set of \(Q\) relative to the interior point \(x\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dimension-controlled universal-barrier existence property
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal Q_n\) denote the class of closed convex sets \(Q\subset\mathbb R^n\) with nonempty interior and no affine line. Let \(\mathcal B_\nu(Q)\) denote the class of \(\nu\)-self-concordant barriers for \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence statement for arbitrary finite-dimensional line-free convex domains; no efficient representation or evaluation oracle is assumed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A class \(\mathcal Q_n\) has the dimension-controlled universal-barrier existence property if there is an absolute constant \(C>0\) such that
\[
\forall Q\in\mathcal Q_n\quad \mathcal B_{Cn}(Q)\ne\varnothing.
\]
The polar-volume construction realizes this property: for every \(Q\in\mathcal Q_n\), there are absolute constants \(c_1,c_2>0\) such that
\[
U_Q(x)=c_1\log\operatorname{vol}_n\{s:\langle s,z-x\rangle\le1\ \forall z\in Q\}
\]
belongs to \(\mathcal B_{c_2n}(Q)\). Thus barrier existence and parameter control depend only linearly on dimension, even when \(Q\) has no supplied algebraic description.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Universal-barrier existence means that every closed, line-free convex domain in \(n\) dimensions has some self-concordant barrier with parameter at most a universal constant times \(n\). The polar-volume barrier establishes this property without requiring polyhedral, semidefinite, or other explicit structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists C>0\) absolute such that \(\forall Q\in\mathcal Q_n\), a \((Cn)\)-self-concordant barrier for \(Q\) exists.
equivalent_formulations_latex:

u:\mathcal B_
u(Q)
e\varnothing\}=O(n)\).
special_cases_latex: Bounded convex bodies satisfy the hypotheses automatically once they have nonempty interior.
A pointed full-dimensional closed cone satisfies the no-line hypothesis and therefore admits a dimension-controlled barrier, although a more structured barrier may be preferable.
immediate_consequences_latex: Lack of an explicit standard cone representation is not an obstruction to abstract barrier existence.
The existence parameter is independent of the number of inequalities in any particular description of \(Q\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-body version of the entropic barrier; additive normalization of Lebesgue measure is immaterial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[A(\theta)=\log\int_K\exp(\langle\theta,z\rangle)\,dz\qquad(\theta\in\mathbb{R}^n).\] Its Fenchel conjugate \[F_K(x)=A^*(x)=\sup_{\theta\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{\langle\theta,x\rangle-A(\theta)\}\] is finite precisely on \(\operatorname{int}K\), diverges as \(x\to\partial K\), and is a self-concordant barrier with parameter bounded by a universal constant times \(n\). At an attained supremum, \(x=\nabla A(\theta)\), so \(x\) is the mean of the corresponding exponentially tilted log-concave distribution.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Entropic barrier as a log-Laplace conjugate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a convex body with nonempty interior and positive finite Lebesgue volume. Pair \(\mathbb R^n\) with its dual by the Euclidean inner product.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex bodies and the continuous uniform base measure; unbounded domains require a different base measure or conic formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the log-Laplace transform of Lebesgue measure restricted to \(K\) by
\[
A_K(\theta)=\log\int_K e^{\langle\theta,x\rangle}\,dx,\qquad \theta\in\mathbb R^n.
\]
Its Fenchel conjugate is
\[
A_K^*(x)=\sup_{\theta\in\mathbb R^n}\{\langle\theta,x\rangle-A_K(\theta)\}.
\]
The entropic universal barrier of \(K\) is
\[
F_{\mathrm{ent},K}(x)=A_K^*(x),\qquad x\in\operatorname{int}K.
\]
Equivalently, when \(x=\nabla A_K(\theta)\), the maximizing parameter is \(\theta=\nabla A_K^*(x)\), and the Hessians satisfy \(\nabla^2A_K^*(x)=[\nabla^2A_K(\theta)]^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The entropic barrier is the convex conjugate of the logarithm of the moment-generating integral of the uniform measure on a convex body. Its natural domain is the body's interior. Primal points are means of exponentially tilted distributions, and the barrier Hessian is the inverse covariance matrix of the corresponding tilt.
assumptions_latex: Lebesgue measure is used as the reference measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_{\mathrm{ent},K}=A_K^*\) on \(\operatorname{int}K\) is the entropic universal-barrier construction associated with \(K\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For density \(p_\theta(x)=\exp(\langle\theta,x\rangle-A_K(\theta))\mathbf1_K(x)\), \(\nabla A_K(\theta)=\mathbb E_\theta[X]\) and \(\nabla^2A_K(\theta)=\operatorname{Cov}_\theta(X)\).
\(A_K^*(x)=\langle\theta,x\rangle-A_K(\theta)\) whenever \(x=\nabla A_K(\theta)\).
special_cases_latex: Changing the reference measure by a positive constant adds a constant to \(A_K\) and subtracts the same constant from \(A_K^*\), leaving derivatives unchanged.
immediate_consequences_latex: The local metric of the entropic barrier is the inverse covariance metric of the exponential family.
Affine images of \(K\) induce the corresponding conjugate barrier up to an additive constant.
boundary_notes: This record does not assert an exact self-concordance parameter because the available local source corpus did not provide an inspectable statement of that theorem.
For unbounded \(K\), the Lebesgue log-Laplace integral need not be finite on all of the dual space.

notation.meaning: Log-Laplace transform of Lebesgue measure on \(K\).

children.title: Universal-Barrier Computability Boundary
children.top_down_role: Separation between barrier existence, parameter quality, and efficient oracle evaluation.

assumptions_latex: A convex domain is supplied only through an abstract membership or separation description.
No integration, sampling, or barrier-evaluation oracle is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Existence of an \(O(n)\)-parameter barrier alone does not furnish a polynomial-time barrier oracle or path-following implementation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: existential representation and oracle implementability are distinct complexity claims
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates geometric existence and parameter quality from algorithmic evaluation under an explicit input model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A theorem asserting an \(O(n)\)-parameter self-concordant barrier \(F\) establishes neither an algorithm for computing \(F(x)\), \(\nabla F(x)\), and \(\nabla^2F(x)\), nor polynomial bounds for those computations. In particular, the polar-volume formula requires volume computation, while the entropic formula requires evaluating or optimizing a log-partition function. Consequently, a polynomial-time path-following claim additionally requires a specified input model and a polynomial-time exact or sufficiently accurate oracle for these quantities; barrier existence alone supplies no such oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A good universal barrier may exist geometrically while its value, gradient, and Hessian remain unavailable through an efficient oracle.
knowledge_statements.title: Universal-Barrier Computability Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and local meaning are appropriate, but a formal input/oracle model and authoritative complexity source are required to support the computational separation claimed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Oracle-computable barrier versus existential barrier
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a convex set \(Q\subset\mathbb R^n\) be supplied through an input representation \(\mathcal R(Q)\). Let \(F:\operatorname{int}Q\to\mathbb R\) be a self-concordant barrier.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computational distinction between mathematical existence and usable second-order barrier access; the input representation and arithmetic model must be specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A barrier \(F\) is second-order oracle computable relative to \(\mathcal R(Q)\) if there is an algorithm which, for every rational interior query \(x\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), returns approximations to
\[
F(x),\qquad \nabla F(x),\qquad \nabla^2F(x)
\]
with prescribed error \(\varepsilon\), in time polynomial in the encoding length of \(\mathcal R(Q)\), \(x\), and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\). A barrier model is Newton-tractable when it additionally permits the required linear systems in \(\nabla^2F(x)\) to be solved within polynomial resource bounds. The universal-barrier computability boundary is the logical separation
\[
\text{existence of a barrier with }\nu=O(n)\quad\not\Rightarrow\quad\text{second-order oracle computability}.
\]
For the polar-volume universal barrier, evaluating a volume and its derivatives is not generally supplied by the existence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A universal barrier can have an excellent dimension-dependent parameter yet still be unusable computationally. It crosses the practical boundary only when its value, gradient, Hessian, and Newton systems can be computed to requested accuracy in polynomial resources relative to the given representation of the convex set.
assumptions_latex: An explicit encoding \(\mathcal R(Q)\) and accuracy model are fixed.
Complexity includes derivative evaluation and Newton-system solution, not only evaluation of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The existence of a \(Cn\)-self-concordant barrier for every line-free \(Q\) does not by itself establish a polynomial-time barrier oracle for \(Q\).
special_cases_latex: For standard logarithmic barriers with explicitly listed affine inequalities, values, gradients, and Hessians are directly computable from the input.
For the polar-volume barrier, the defining volume may encode a substantially harder subproblem.
immediate_consequences_latex: Barrier parameter quality and per-iteration cost are separate complexity attributes.
An iteration bound expressed only through \(\nu\) is not an end-to-end running-time guarantee.
boundary_notes: The definition is relative to an input representation; a barrier can be tractable under one representation and intractable under another.
No unconditional hardness classification for a particular volume oracle is asserted here.

notation.meaning: Chosen finite representation of the convex set.
Cost of solving a barrier-Hessian Newton system.
