knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fenchel duality of nondegenerate self-concordant barriers
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(E\) be finite-dimensional with dual \(E^*\). Let \(F:\operatorname{dom}F\to\mathbb R\) be closed, strictly convex, self-concordant, with open domain containing no affine line and with \(\nabla^2F(x)\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Legendre-type finite-dimensional self-concordant functions; conic sign conventions are deferred to the dual-cone construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Fenchel-dual barrier function is
\[
F_*(s)=\sup_{x\in\operatorname{dom}F}\{\langle s,x\rangle-F(x)\},
\qquad s\in\operatorname{dom}F_*.
\]
Barrier duality pairs \(x\) and \(s\) by
\[
s=\nabla F(x),\qquad x=\nabla F_*(s).
\]
At every such pair,
\[
\nabla^2F_*(s)=[\nabla^2F(x)]^{-1}.
\]
The dual function is self-concordant with the same self-concordance constant as \(F\). Hence the gradient map is a diffeomorphism from \(\operatorname{dom}F\) onto \(\operatorname{dom}F_*\), and primal and dual local metrics are inverse descriptions of the same pairing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Barrier duality is Fenchel conjugacy specialized to a nondegenerate self-concordant function. The primal gradient identifies the dual point, the dual gradient returns the primal point, and the two Hessians are inverses. Self-concordance is preserved under this operation.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is closed, strictly convex, and self-concordant on an open domain.
The domain contains no affine line.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
For \(s=
abla F(x)\), \(
abla F_*(s)=x\), \(
abla^2F_*(s)=[
abla^2F(x)]^{-1}\), and \(F_*\) has the same self-concordance constant as \(F\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(F(x)+F_*(s)=\langle s,x\rangle\) if and only if \(s=\nabla F(x)\).
\(\nabla F_*=(\nabla F)^{-1}\) on the respective open domains.
special_cases_latex: For \(F(x)=-\sum_i\log x_i\) on \(\mathbb R_{++}^n\), \(\operatorname{dom}F_*=\mathbb R_{--}^n\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The primal local norm and dual local norm coincide under the Hessian identification.
Dikin ellipsoids in dual gradient coordinates are governed by the inverse primal Hessian.
boundary_notes: If the Hessian is singular, the inverse-Hessian formulation requires restriction to the effective affine hull or a generalized formulation.
For a barrier on a positive cone, the ordinary conjugate lives on the negative dual cone; a sign change produces a barrier on the positive dual cone.

notation.meaning: Dual point paired with \(x\) by \(s=\nabla F(x)\).
Algebraic dual of the finite-dimensional space \(E\).

children.title: Dual-Cone Barrier Construction
children.top_down_role: Passage from a conic barrier to its conjugate barrier on the dual cone.

assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a regular cone and \(K^*=\{s:\langle s,x\rangle\ge0\ \forall x\in K\}\).
\(F\) is a \(\nu\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier on \(\operatorname{int}K\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard conjugacy theorem for logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the positive-dual-cone convention and the corresponding sign-adjusted Fenchel conjugate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \[F_*(s)=\sup_{x\in\operatorname{int}K}\{-\langle s,xangle-F(x)\}.\] Then \(F_*\) is a \(
u\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier on \(\operatorname{int}K^*\). For every \(x\in\operatorname{int}K\), the point \(s=-
abla F(x)\) lies in \(\operatorname{int}K^*\), attains the conjugate pairing, and satisfies \(-
abla F_*(s)=x\). Thus conjugation transfers the barrier without increasing its parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A logarithmically homogeneous conic barrier yields a barrier with the same parameter on the positive dual cone by sign-adjusted conjugation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sign-adjusted conjugate barrier on the dual cone
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\subset E\) be a closed, pointed, full-dimensional convex cone and \(K^*=\{y\in E^*:\langle y,x\rangle\ge0\ \forall x\in K\}\). Let \(F\) be a nondegenerate \(\nu\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier on \(\operatorname{int}K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional logarithmically homogeneous conic barriers and the positive-dual convention for \(K^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
F_*(s)=\sup_{x\in\operatorname{int}K}\{\langle s,x\rangle-F(x)\},
\qquad s\in-\operatorname{int}K^*.
\]
The dual-cone barrier induced by \(F\) is the sign-adjusted conjugate
\[
F^\dagger(y)=F_*(-y)=\sup_{x\in\operatorname{int}K}\{-\langle y,x\rangle-F(x)\},
\qquad y\in\operatorname{int}K^*.
\]
The primal-dual point associated with \(x\in\operatorname{int}K\) is \(y=-\nabla F(x)\). At this pair,
\[
\nabla F^\dagger(y)=-x,
\qquad
\nabla^2F^\dagger(y)=[\nabla^2F(x)]^{-1}.
\]
Moreover, \(F^\dagger\) is logarithmically homogeneous of degree \(\nu\), up to the additive normalization inherited from conjugacy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ordinary Fenchel conjugate of a logarithmically homogeneous barrier on \(K\) is naturally defined on the negative dual cone. Composing it with the sign map yields a barrier on the positive dual cone. The pairing is \(y=-\nabla F(x)\), and the dual Hessian is the inverse primal Hessian.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a nondegenerate \(\nu\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier on \(\operatorname{int}K\).
The dual cone uses the convention \(\langle y,x\rangle\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(F^\dagger(y)=F_*(-y)\) defines the conjugate barrier on \(\operatorname{int}K^*\), with \(
abla^2F^\dagger(-
abla F(x))=[
abla^2F(x)]^{-1}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(y=-\nabla F(x)\iff x=-\nabla F^\dagger(y)\).
\(F(x)+F^\dagger(y)=-\langle y,x\rangle\) at paired points.
special_cases_latex: For \(K=\mathbb R_+^n\) and \(F(x)=-\sum_i\log x_i\), the dual construction gives \(F^\dagger(y)=-\sum_i\log y_i\) up to an additive constant.
immediate_consequences_latex: The gradient map \(-\nabla F\) sends \(\operatorname{int}K\) onto \(\operatorname{int}K^*\).
Primal and dual barrier parameters agree under conjugacy.
boundary_notes: The sign in \(F^\dagger(y)=F_*(-y)\) is essential under the positive-dual convention.
The construction assumes Legendre nondegeneracy; degenerate cones require passage to their linear span.
review_flags: The positive-dual sign adjustment is an explicit convention combining the cited Fenchel and logarithmic-homogeneity statements.
knowledge_statements.title: Sign-adjusted conjugate barrier on the dual cone

children.title: Primal–Dual Metric Pairing
children.top_down_role: Relationships between local metrics on paired cone interiors.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(F_*\) are the paired barriers of the dual-cone construction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla^2F_*(s)=[\nabla^2F(x)]^{-1}\), so primal and dual local norms are paired isometrically.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Hessian inversion under smooth Legendre conjugacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric identity at gradient-paired primal and dual interior points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H_x=
abla^2F(x)\) and let \(s=-
abla F(x)\). Differentiating the inverse gradient correspondence gives \[
abla^2F_*(s)=H_x^{-1}.\] Hence, for \(h\) in the primal space and \(u\) in its dual, \[\|h\|_x^2=\langle H_xh,hangle,\qquad \|u\|_{*,s}^2=\langle u,H_x^{-1}uangle.\] In particular, the Hessian map is an isometry in the sense that \(\|H_xh\|_{*,s}=\|h\|_x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At gradient-paired points, the dual barrier Hessian is the inverse primal Hessian, and their local norms match through the Hessian map.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Metric Pairing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inverse-Hessian metric identity fits the property leaf, but a source must establish the needed smooth Legendre correspondence for the paired barriers.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inverse-Hessian pairing of primal and dual local metrics
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F\) and \(F^\dagger\) be a nondegenerate conjugate pair of conic barriers on \(\operatorname{int}K\) and \(\operatorname{int}K^*\). Pair \(x\) and \(y\) by \(y=-\nabla F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Riemannian norms at exactly conjugate primal-dual points; arbitrary unpaired points are not covered.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set
\[
H_x=\nabla^2F(x),\qquad H_y^\dagger=\nabla^2F^\dagger(y).
\]
The primal-dual metric pairing at \(y=-\nabla F(x)\) is the inverse relation
\[
H_y^\dagger=H_x^{-1}.
\]
Consequently, for \(u\in E\) and \(v\in E^*\), define
\[
\|u\|_x^2=\langle H_xu,u\rangle,
\qquad
\|v\|_{y,\dagger}^2=\langle v,H_y^\dagger v\rangle.
\]
Then the Hessian identification is an isometry:
\[
\|H_xu\|_{y,\dagger}=\|u\|_x,

aqquad
\|H_y^\dagger v\|_x=\|v\|_{y,\dagger}.
\]
Thus the primal tangent metric and dual cotangent metric encode the same quadratic geometry at conjugate points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At points paired by the barrier gradient, the dual barrier Hessian is exactly the inverse of the primal barrier Hessian. Applying the primal Hessian to a primal direction preserves its norm when the result is measured in the dual metric, and conversely for the dual Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla^2F^\dagger(y)=[\nabla^2F(x)]^{-1}\), and the Hessian maps are mutual isometries between the paired local norms.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For all \(u\in E\), \(\langle H_xu,H_y^\dagger H_xu\rangle=\langle H_xu,u\rangle\).
For all \(v\in E^*\), \(\langle H_y^\dagger v,H_xH_y^\dagger v\rangle=\langle v,H_y^\dagger v\rangle\).
special_cases_latex: For the orthant barrier, \(H_x=\operatorname{Diag}(x_i^{-2})\) and the paired point is \(y_i=x_i^{-1}\), so \(H_y^\dagger=\operatorname{Diag}(x_i^2)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The unit Dikin ellipsoid at \(x\) maps under \(H_x\) to the unit dual Dikin ellipsoid at \(y\).
Newton directions may be expressed equivalently in primal or paired dual coordinates.
boundary_notes: The identity is exact only at conjugate points; Hessians at independently chosen \(x\) and \(y\) need not be inverses.
This metric pairing does not assert the stronger existence of a self-scaled scaling point for every arbitrary pair.

notation.meaning: Dual barrier Hessian at the conjugate point \(y\).
Local norm induced by the dual barrier Hessian.

review_flags: The norm-isometry equations are the direct metric formulation of the cited inverse-Hessian identity.

children.title: Self-Scaled Metric Matching
children.top_down_role: Specialized symmetric-cone geometry underlying scaling points.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a unique scaling point \(w\in\operatorname{int}K\) satisfying \(\nabla^2F(w)x=s\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: defining metric-matching property of self-scaled barriers on symmetric cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Self-scaled-barrier metric matching; this specialized property characterizes symmetric-cone scaling geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every primal-dual pair \((x,s)\in\operatorname{int}K\times\operatorname{int}K^*\), there exists a unique \(w\in\operatorname{int}K\) such that \[H_wx=s,\qquad H_w=\nabla^2F(w).\] The positive-definite map \(H_w\) sends \(K\) onto \(K^*\) and identifies the local primal and dual metrics. The point \(w\) is the scaling point of \((x,s)\); its existence for every interior pair is special to self-scaled barriers and the associated symmetric-cone geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A self-scaled barrier supplies a unique point whose Hessian maps any chosen primal interior point to its paired dual point.
knowledge_statements.title: Self-Scaled Metric Matching

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nesterov–Todd scaling point and matched metric
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\subset E\) be a pointed convex cone with nonempty interior and let \(F\) be a self-scaled barrier for \(K\). Let \(K^*\subset E^*\) be the dual cone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specialized self-scaled geometry, available for symmetric-cone barrier structures rather than arbitrary self-concordant barriers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any \(x\in\operatorname{int}K\) and \(s\in\operatorname{int}K^*\), the self-scaled metric-matching point is the unique \(w\in\operatorname{int}K\) satisfying
\[
\nabla^2F(w)x=s.
\]
The positive-definite operator
\[
T_w=[\nabla^2F(w)]^{1/2}
\]
is the associated scaling map. It matches the pair because
\[
T_wx=T_w^{-1}s,
\]
where the adjoint identification is understood between \(E\) and \(E^*\). Equivalently, the single Hessian metric at \(w\) transports the primal point \(x\) to the dual point \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A self-scaled barrier assigns every interior primal-dual pair a unique scaling point \(w\). The Hessian at \(w\) maps the primal point to the dual point. Its positive square root places both points at the same location in scaled coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a unique \(w\in\operatorname{int}K\) with \(\nabla^2F(w)x=s\); for \(T_w=[\nabla^2F(w)]^{1/2}\), \(T_wx=T_w^{-1}s\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(s=H_wx\) with \(H_w=\nabla^2F(w)\).
\(T_w^2x=s\) and hence \(T_wx=T_w^{-1}s\).
special_cases_latex: For \(K=\mathbb R_+^n\) and \(F(x)=-\sum_i\log x_i\), \(w_i=\sqrt{x_i/s_i}\).
For the positive-semidefinite cone, metric matching yields the matrix Nesterov–Todd scaling.
immediate_consequences_latex: The primal and dual variables have identical scaled representatives.
The scaling point supplies a symmetric local metric used by primal-dual search directions.
boundary_notes: General nonsymmetric cones need not admit a self-scaled barrier or such a scaling point for every pair.
The equation is stronger than inverse-Hessian pairing at conjugate points because \(x\) and \(s\) are arbitrary interior points.

notation.meaning: Positive square root of the barrier Hessian at \(w\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Barrier-generated analytic center
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\subset E\) be a convex set with nonempty interior, and let \(F:\operatorname{int}Q\to\mathbb R\) be a closed, differentiable, strictly convex barrier.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier-relative centers in finite dimensions; the center depends on the chosen barrier and need not exist on an unnormalized unbounded domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An analytic center of \(Q\) generated by \(F\) is a point
\[
x_F^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\operatorname{int}Q}F(x).
\]
When \(F\) is differentiable and strictly convex, existence implies uniqueness and the center is characterized by
\[
\nabla F(x_F^*)=0.
\]
If \(F\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier and the center exists, its local Hessian metric defines the center Dikin ellipsoid and satisfies the global localization bound
\[
\|x-x_F^*\|_{x_F^*}\le \nu+2\sqrt\nu,
\qquad x\in Q,
\]
while \(\{x_F^*+h:\|h\|_{x_F^*}<1\}\subset\operatorname{int}Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The analytic center is the minimizer of a selected barrier over the feasible interior. Strict convexity makes it unique, and differentiability makes zero barrier gradient its stationarity certificate. For a self-concordant barrier, the Hessian at the center also provides an inner Dikin ellipsoid and a parameter-controlled outer localization.
assumptions_latex: For the metric bounds, \(F\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier and \(x_F^*\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_F^*=\arg\min_{x\in\operatorname{int}Q}F(x)\) is the barrier-generated analytic center, with \(\nabla F(x_F^*)=0\) under differentiability.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For differentiable convex \(F\), \(x_F^*\) is an analytic center if and only if \(0=\nabla F(x_F^*)\), provided a minimizer exists.
\(x_F^*\) is the zero-penalty endpoint of the central path generated by \(F\).
special_cases_latex: For \(Q=\{x:a_i^Tx<b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(F(x)=-\sum_i\log(b_i-a_i^Tx)\), the center satisfies \(\sum_i a_i/(b_i-a_i^Tx_F^*)=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The analytic center is barrier-dependent rather than an affine-free center of the set alone.
The center Hessian supplies a canonical local norm for localization and initialization.
boundary_notes: A logarithmically homogeneous barrier on an unsliced cone has no finite minimizer because scaling decreases the barrier without bound.
If the barrier is not strictly convex, the argmin can contain more than one point.

source_refs.locator: §5.3.3, Definition 5.3.3 and Theorem 5.3.9, pp. 376–377

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A barrier path based at an interior point and driven by the negative initial barrier gradient; the definition presupposes that the displayed minimizer is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a self-concordant barrier and fix \(y_0\in\operatorname{dom}F\). For \(t\ge0\), whenever the displayed minimizer exists, define the auxiliary central path by \(y^*(t)=\arg\min_{y\in\operatorname{dom}F}\{-t\langle\nabla F(y_0),y\rangle+F(y)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given an interior point, the auxiliary central path is defined by minimizing the barrier after tilting it by minus t times the initial barrier gradient, whenever that minimizer is attained.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Epigraph Analytic-Center Cutting-Plane Algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An analytic-center cutting-plane scheme for convex minimization over a full-dimensional polytope; no convergence guarantee is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min\{u:w\in C,\ \Psi(w)\le u\}\), where \(C=\{w:a_i^\top w\le b_i,\ i\in I_0\}\) has nonempty interior and \(g_t\in\partial\Psi(w_{t-1})\) is available. Initialize \(w_0\) as the analytic center of \(C\) and the incumbent upper bound \(U_0=+\infty\). For \(t\ge1\), add the valid epigraph cut
\[
u\ge \Psi(w_{t-1})+g_t^\top(w-w_{t-1}).
\]
At \(t=1\), also impose \(u\le\Psi(w_0)\); subsequently replace the incumbent upper-bound cut \(u\le U_{t-1}\) by \(u\le U_t:=\Psi(w_{t-1})\) whenever \(\Psi(w_{t-1})\le U_{t-1}\). Choose the next query point \((w_t,u_t)\) as the analytic center of the resulting localization polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Form an epigraph model over a full-dimensional polytope. At each iteration, evaluate the convex objective and a subgradient at the preceding analytic center, add the corresponding supporting epigraph cut, tighten the objective upper-bound cut whenever a better value is found, and take the analytic center of the updated localization polytope as the next iterate.
assumptions_latex: C=\{w:a_i^\top w\le b_i,\ i\in I_0\}\text{ is a polytope with }\operatorname{int}C\ne\varnothing
g_t\in\partial\Psi(w_{t-1})\text{ is available at each iteration}
\text{Each updated localization polytope admits an analytic center}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Analytic center of a linear matrix inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is the log-determinant-barrier specialization of analytic centers for semidefinite generalized inequalities. Strict feasibility defines a nonempty barrier domain but does not by itself assert that the minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let A_1,\ldots,A_n,B be symmetric matrices of a common size, and suppose
\[
\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:B-\sum_{j=1}^n x_jA_j\succ0\right\}\neq\varnothing.
\]
An analytic center of the linear matrix inequality \sum_{j=1}^n x_jA_j\preceq B is any point
\[
x_{\mathrm{ac}}\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{B-\sum_{j=1}^n x_jA_j\succ0}-\log\det\left(B-\sum_{j=1}^n x_jA_j\right),
\]
whenever this argmin is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a strictly feasible linear matrix inequality, an analytic center is any minimizer of the negative log determinant of its positive-definite matrix slack. Strict feasibility alone supplies the barrier domain and does not guarantee attainment.
assumptions_latex: A_1,\ldots,A_n,B\text{ are symmetric matrices of a common size}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constrained Analytic Center
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the barrier-induced center of a bounded convex intersection with nonempty barrier interior under the stated lineality and Hessian-nondegeneracy assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\subset\mathbb E\) be closed and convex and contain no straight lines. Let \(F\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier for \(Q\) whose Hessian is nondegenerate on \(\operatorname{int}Q\), and let \(\widehat P\subset\mathbb E\) be closed and convex. Define
\[
P=\widehat P\cap Q,\qquad P_0=\widehat P\cap\operatorname{int}Q.
\]
If \(P\) is bounded and \(P_0\ne\varnothing\), the constrained analytic center of \(P\) with respect to \(F\) is
\[
x_0=\arg\min_{x\in P_0}F(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a bounded intersection of a closed convex constraint set with a line-free barrier domain, provided the intersection meets the domain interior, the constrained analytic center is the minimizer of the self-concordant barrier over that interior feasible section.
assumptions_latex: Q\subset\mathbb E\text{ is closed and convex and contains no straight lines}
\widehat P\subset\mathbb E\text{ is closed and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_0=\arg\min_{x\in P_0}F(x)\text{ is the constrained analytic center of }P\text{ with respect to }F.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Hessian Comparison with the Analytic-Center Metric
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A bounded-domain comparison between local dual norms, equivalently between barrier Hessians.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier with bounded domain and analytic center \(x_F^*\). Then, for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}F\) and every \(p\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[
\|p\|_x^*\le (\nu+2\sqrt\nu)\|p\|_{x_F^*}^*.
\]
Equivalently, for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}F\),
\[
\nabla^2F(x)\succeq \frac{1}{(\nu+2\sqrt\nu)^2}\nabla^2F(x_F^*).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a bounded domain, the dual local norm at any point is at most nu plus twice the square root of nu times the dual norm at the analytic center. Equivalently, every barrier Hessian uniformly dominates the analytic-center Hessian by the reciprocal squared factor.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Damped Newton method for analytic centers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The algorithm and its local-dual-norm stopping test are reproduced without adding an unstated convergence guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(y_0\in\operatorname{dom}F\). For \(k\geq0\), set \[y_{k+1}=y_k-\frac{[F''(y_k)]^{-1}F'(y_k)}{1+\|F'(y_k)\|_{y_k}^*}.\] Stop when \(\|F'(y_k)\|_{y_k}^*\leq\beta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a point in the barrier domain, take Newton steps damped by one plus the local dual norm of the gradient, and stop when that norm is at most beta.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Analytic center of convex inequalities and affine equalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is an inequality-representation-dependent center. Strict feasibility supplies the barrier domain; the boundedness statement concerns boundedness below and does not independently assert attainment. Affine coordinate invariance is understood covariantly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R} be convex for i=1,\ldots,m, and suppose \{x:Fx=g,\ f_i(x)<0\ \forall i\}\neq\varnothing. An analytic center of this inequality-and-equality representation is any point
\[
x_{\mathrm{ac}}\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{Fx=g,\ f_i(x)<0}\left(-\sum_{i=1}^m\log(-f_i(x))\right).
\]
Equivalently, it maximizes \prod_{i=1}^m(-f_i(x)) over the strictly feasible affine set. If that set is bounded, the logarithmic barrier is bounded below. The center can change under a different inequality representation of the same set. Under an invertible affine change of coordinates it transforms with the coordinates, and it is unchanged by positive rescalings f_i\mapsto\alpha_i f_i with \alpha_i>0 or by replacing Fx=g with an equivalent equality representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An analytic center minimizes the logarithmic barrier of a strictly feasible system of convex inequalities and affine equalities, equivalently maximizing the product of its inequality slacks. A bounded strictly feasible set makes the barrier bounded below. The center depends on the chosen inequalities, but transforms consistently under invertible affine coordinate changes and is unaffected by positive constraint scaling or an equivalent rewriting of the equalities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A damped Newton iteration and stopping test for barrier minimization; the extract does not itself assert finite termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier and choose \(y_0\in\operatorname{dom}F\). For \(k\ge0\), define \(\lambda_k=\|
abla F(y_k)\|_{y_k}^*\), \(\xi_k=\lambda_k^2/(1+\lambda_k)\), and \(y_{k+1}=y_k-(1+\xi_k)^{-1}[
abla^2F(y_k)]^{-1}
abla F(y_k)\). Stop when \(\lambda_k\le eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from an interior point, repeatedly take the stated damped Newton step for the barrier and stop when the barrier gradient's local dual norm is at most beta. This algorithm statement alone does not guarantee that the stopping test will be reached.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Analytic center induced by a logarithmic barrier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the representation-dependent analytic center for a continuously inequality-described set. Existence and uniqueness of a minimizer are not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb E^n\), let \(g_j:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) be continuous for \(j=1,\ldots,m\), and define \(\mathcal S=\{x\in\mathcal X:g_j(x)\geq 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\). Assume \(\mathcal S_{++}=\{x\in\mathcal X:g_j(x)>0\ \text{for every }j\}\neq\varnothing\). Define \(\psi(x)=-\sum_{j=1}^m\log g_j(x)\) on \(\mathcal S_{++}\). The analytic center associated with this inequality representation is the vector or set of vectors minimizing \(\psi\) over \(\mathcal S_{++}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a set represented by continuous inequalities with a nonempty strictly feasible region, define the logarithmic potential as the negative sum of the logarithms of the constraint functions. The minimizers of this potential over the strictly feasible region form the analytic center associated with that representation; attainment and uniqueness are not guaranteed by the stated assumptions.
assumptions_latex: g_j:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\text{ is continuous for }j=1,\ldots,m

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Analytic Center of a Polytope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation-dependent logarithmic-barrier definition for a polytope with nonempty interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let E_k=\{x\in\mathbb R^n\mid \langle a_j,x\rangle\le b_j,\ j=1,\ldots,m_k\} have nonempty interior, and define F_k(x)=-\sum_{j=1}^{m_k}\ln\bigl(b_j-\langle a_j,x\rangle\bigr) on \operatorname{int}(E_k). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the specified inequality representation of a polytope with nonempty interior, an analytic center is any interior minimizer of the logarithmic barrier formed from the constraint slacks.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Analytic center of a linear-inequality representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is the polyhedral specialization of the logarithmic-barrier analytic center. Boundedness and strict feasibility support the stated uniqueness conclusion; nonzero normals are additionally required for the hyperplane-distance interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_i^Tx\le b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}
\]
have a strictly feasible point. Its inequality-representation analytic center is any solution of
\[
\operatorname*{minimize}_{b_i-a_i^Tx>0}\left(-\sum_{i=1}^m\log(b_i-a_i^Tx)\right).
\]
If P is bounded, this barrier is bounded below and strictly convex, so the analytic center is unique. For nonzero a_i, positive rescaling permits \|a_i\|_2=1; then b_i-a_i^Tx is the Euclidean distance from x to \{z:a_i^Tz=b_i\}, and the analytic center maximizes the product of these distances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The analytic center of a strictly feasible linear-inequality representation minimizes the sum of negative logarithms of its slacks. If the represented polyhedron is bounded, the barrier is bounded below and strictly convex, so the center is unique. After normalizing nonzero constraint normals, the center maximizes the product of distances to the defining hyperplanes.
assumptions_latex: P\text{ is bounded for the uniqueness conclusion}
a_i\neq0\ \forall i\text{ for the hyperplane-distance interpretation}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Analytic center on a bounded barrier domain
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\subset E\) be a bounded closed convex set with nonempty interior. Let \(F:\operatorname{int}Q\to\mathbb R\) be a closed, strictly convex barrier, such as a nondegenerate self-concordant barrier.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional bounded feasible interiors; relative-interior formulations require first restricting to the affine hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The bounded-domain analytic center generated by \(F\) is
\[
x_F^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\operatorname{int}Q}F(x).
\]
Because \(Q\) is bounded and \(F\) is closed with barrier growth at the boundary, the minimum is attained in \(\operatorname{int}Q\); strict convexity makes it unique. It is equivalently the unique solution of
\[
\nabla F(x)=0.
\]
If \(F\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier, the point is also the initial point of the exact central path
\[
x^*(t)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\operatorname{int}Q}\{t\langle c,x\rangle+F(x)\},
\qquad x^*(0)=x_F^*.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a bounded closed convex domain, a closed strictly convex barrier attains a unique interior minimum. This minimum is the bounded-domain analytic center, is characterized by zero gradient, and is the zero-penalty starting point of the barrier central path.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is bounded, closed, and convex with \(\operatorname{int}Q\ne\varnothing\).
\(F\) is closed and tends to \(+\infty\) at the boundary of \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a unique \(x_F^*\in\operatorname{int}Q\) minimizing \(F\), and \(\nabla F(x_F^*)=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x_F^*=x^*(0)\) for the central path generated by \(F\).
For a polyhedral logarithmic barrier, \(x_F^*\) maximizes the product of the positive slacks.
special_cases_latex: For \(F(x)=-\sum_{i=1}^m\log(b_i-a_i^Tx)\), minimizing \(F\) is equivalent to maximizing \(\prod_{i=1}^m(b_i-a_i^Tx)\) over the strict interior.
immediate_consequences_latex: No external normalization is needed when the barrier domain itself is bounded.
The center supplies a strictly feasible initialization whenever it can be computed.
boundary_notes: Boundedness is a sufficient domain condition; some unbounded domains may admit minima for nonhomogeneous barriers, but not under the full hypotheses used for the standard localization result.
A bounded set with empty ambient interior must be treated in its affine hull.

children.title: Normalized Conic Centers
children.top_down_role: Center notions obtained after slicing homogeneous domains.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a regular cone and \(F\) is a logarithmically homogeneous barrier on \(\operatorname{int}K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A normalized conic center is a minimizer of \(F\) over \(S_e\), satisfying \(\nabla F(x_e)+\lambda e=0\).

notation.meaning: normalized affine slice of the cone

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conic centers require a bounded affine normalization because logarithmic homogeneity precludes an unconstrained minimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Center obtained by intersecting a homogeneous cone with a bounded affine normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because logarithmic homogeneity prevents \(F\) from having an unconstrained minimizer on \(K\), fix \(e\in\operatorname{int}K^*\) and minimize over \[S_e=\{x\in\operatorname{int}K:\langle e,x\rangle=1\}.\] A normalized conic center is \[x_e\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in S_e}F(x).\] When the minimum exists and \(F\) is strictly convex on the slice, it is unique. Its first-order condition is \(\nabla F(x_e)+\lambda e=0\) for some \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Analytic center of a normalized cone slice
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\subset E\) be a closed, pointed, full-dimensional convex cone, let \(e\in\operatorname{int}K^*\), and let \(F\) be a nondegenerate \(\nu\)-logarithmically homogeneous barrier on \(\operatorname{int}K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous conic domains after an interior dual functional fixes scale; the unsliced cone has no finite analytic center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The \(e\)-normalized cone slice is
\[
S_e=\{x\in\operatorname{int}K:\langle e,x\rangle=1\}.
\]
Its normalized conic center is
\[
x_{F,e}^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in S_e}F(x).
\]
When the slice is nonempty and the restricted barrier is strictly convex, this center is unique. Its first-order characterization is
\[
\nabla F(x_{F,e}^*)+\lambda e=0,
\qquad \langle e,x_{F,e}^*\rangle=1.
\]
Logarithmic homogeneity gives \(\langle\nabla F(x),x\rangle=-\nu\), so necessarily \(\lambda=\nu\). Hence the normalized center is equivalently characterized by
\[
-\nabla F(x_{F,e}^*)=\nu e,
\qquad \langle e,x_{F,e}^*\rangle=1.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone has no preferred scale, so a center is defined after slicing it by an interior dual functional. The normalized conic center minimizes the logarithmically homogeneous barrier on the slice \(\langle e,x\rangle=1\). It is the unique point whose negative barrier gradient equals \(\nu e\).
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a strictly convex \(\nu\)-logarithmically homogeneous barrier on \(\operatorname{int}K\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(y=-\nabla F(x)\), the center is the point paired with the dual ray representative \(y=\nu e\).
Changing the slice to \(\langle e,x\rangle=\rho>0\) scales the center to \(\rho x_{F,e}^*\).
special_cases_latex: For \(K=\mathbb R_+^n\), \(F(x)=-\sum_i\log x_i\), and \(e=\mathbf1\), the normalized center is \(x_i=1/n\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Normalization removes the radial direction along which a logarithmically homogeneous barrier decreases without bound.
The center is covariant under simultaneous primal and dual affine cone isomorphisms.
boundary_notes: If \(e\notin\operatorname{int}K^*\), the slice can be empty or unbounded and a finite center need not exist.
The normalization functional is part of the definition; different \(e\) generally produce different centers.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(0\le\beta<1\), a point \(\bar x\in\operatorname{int}Q\) is a \(\beta\)-approximate analytic center of \(F\) if

children.top_down_role: Unboundedness, recession directions, and normalization failures preventing a finite center.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a \(\nu\)-logarithmically homogeneous barrier on the interior of a regular cone \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unconstrained conic problem \(\inf_{x\in\operatorname{int}K}F(x)\) has value \(-\infty\) and no analytic center.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in\operatorname{int}K\) and \(t>0\), logarithmic homogeneity gives \[F(tx)=F(x)-\nu\log t.\] Therefore \(F(tx)\to-\infty\) as \(t\to+\infty\), so \(F\) has no finite unconstrained minimizer on \(\operatorname{int}K\). More generally, an unbounded feasible domain cannot have a barrier-defined center whenever a recession ray keeps the iterates feasible and the barrier values fail to rise along that ray. A bounded normalization removes this scaling obstruction only if the resulting slice is nonempty and bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unsliced logarithmically homogeneous cone has no analytic center because scaling to infinity drives its barrier value to minus infinity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-center existence and normalization boundary
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\operatorname{dom}F\to\mathbb R\) be a closed nondegenerate self-concordant barrier on an open convex domain containing no affine line.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact analytic centers; distinguishes bounded domains, recession behavior, and homogeneous conic scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the center-existence status of \(F\) by
\[
\mathsf{Center}(F)=
\begin{cases}
\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\operatorname{dom}F}F(x),&\text{if the minimum is attained},\\
\varnothing,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
For a self-concordant function on a line-free domain, boundedness below is the decisive finite-center boundary: if \(\inf F> -\infty\), the minimum is attained uniquely; if \(F\) is unbounded below, no analytic center exists. In particular, a \(\nu\)-logarithmically homogeneous cone barrier satisfies
\[
F(\tau x)=F(x)-\nu\log\tau,
\]
so \(F(\tau x)\to-\infty\) as \(\tau\to\infty\) and the unsliced cone has no finite center. A bounded barrier domain, by contrast, yields a unique center under closedness and strict convexity. Conic centers therefore require a bounded or otherwise coercive normalization slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite analytic center exists precisely when the barrier attains a lower bound. For the standard nondegenerate self-concordant setting, being bounded below guarantees a unique minimizer. Logarithmically homogeneous cone barriers violate this condition along every positive ray, so a cone must be sliced or otherwise normalized before a finite center can be defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathsf{Center}(F)\ne\varnothing\) when \(F\) is bounded below; an unsliced logarithmically homogeneous cone barrier has \(\mathsf{Center}(F)=\varnothing\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under the stated hypotheses, \(\mathsf{Center}(F)\ne\varnothing\iff\inf_{x\in\operatorname{dom}F}F(x)>-\infty\).
For a differentiable strictly convex barrier, center existence is equivalent to solvability of \(\nabla F(x)=0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\operatorname{dom}F\) is bounded, closedness and barrier growth yield a unique center.
If \(F\) is logarithmically homogeneous on a cone, radial scaling prevents a center until a slice such as \(\langle e,x\rangle=1\) is imposed.
immediate_consequences_latex: A failure of center existence can be geometric rather than numerical.
Approximate-center certificates cannot be driven to zero on an unnormalized logarithmically homogeneous cone.
boundary_notes: The equivalence uses the self-concordant, nondegenerate, line-free hypotheses; arbitrary convex functions can be bounded below without attaining their infimum.
Unboundedness of the domain alone is not a complete obstruction for a general nonhomogeneous barrier.

notation.meaning: Singleton exact center when attained, and the empty set otherwise.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The barrier parameter of \(F\) is the least \(\nu\ge0\) such that, for every \(x\in\operatorname{int}Q\) and \(u\in E\),
\[

\le \nu\,\langle\nabla^2F(x)u,u\rangle.

\[

\left\langle\nabla F(x),[\nabla^2F(x)]^{-1}\nabla F(x)\right\rangle
\]

\[

\]

For \(t\ge0\), define \[x(t):=\arg\min_{x\in\operatorname{int}Q}\{t\langle c,xangle+F(x)\},\qquad tc+
abla F(x(t))=0.\] The path-complexity interpretation of \(

u}{t}\] and \[N(\epsilon)=O\!\left(\sqrt

children.title: Barrier-Parameter Calculus
children.top_down_role: Behavior of barrier quality under standard domain and representation operations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closure calculus for self-concordant-barrier parameters
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For each open convex domain \(D_i\) in a finite-dimensional space, let \(F_i:D_i\to\mathbb R\) be a \(\nu_i\)-self-concordant barrier. Parameters below are admissible upper bounds, not necessarily minimal values.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional standard self-concordant barriers under finite sums, affine pullbacks, epigraph lifting, and partial minimization with attained unique minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Barrier-parameter calculus is the collection of closure rules assigning an admissible parameter to a barrier constructed from known barriers. Its basic rules are: (i) on a nonempty intersection, \[F=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 
u(F)\le\sum_{i=1}^m
u_i;\] (ii) for an affine map \(\mathcal A(x)=Ax+b\), \[F\circ\mathcal A\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 
u(F\circ\mathcal A)\le
u(F);\] (iii) for the epigraph construction, \[\widehat F(x,s)=F(x)-\log(s-F(x))\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 
u(\widehat F)\le
u(F)+1;\] and (iv) if \(\Phi(x,y)\) has parameter \(
u\) and \(y(x)\) is the unique attained minimizer, then \[G(x)=\min_y\Phi(x,y)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 
u(G)\le
u.\] These assignments permit parameters to be propagated through explicit formulations without recomputing the defining gradient inequality from scratch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Barrier-parameter calculus consists of closure rules for barriers built from other barriers. Parameters add when barriers are summed over intersected constraints or independent blocks. An affine pullback does not increase the inherited parameter. The standard epigraph lift adds one. Partial minimization over uniquely attained auxiliary variables preserves the parameter upper bound. Every resulting number is an admissible upper bound and can exceed the smallest possible parameter of the resulting domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
The calculus maps sums, affine pullbacks, epigraph lifts, and admissible partial minimizations to the parameter bounds \(\sum_i
u_i\), \(
u\), \(
u+1\), and \(
u\), respectively.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The sum rule covers intersections in one space and Cartesian products after coordinate pullback.
An affine slice is the pullback by the inclusion map of the affine subspace.
special_cases_latex: The logarithmic barrier \(-\sum_{i=1}^m\log(b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x)\) for a polyhedron has the calculus bound \(\nu=m\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Repeated epigraph lifting adds one parameter unit per standard lift.
Eliminating auxiliary variables by admissible partial minimization cannot worsen the inherited parameter bound.
boundary_notes: The calculus gives representation-dependent upper bounds and does not establish parameter optimality.
The partial-minimization rule requires the regularity and attainment conditions stated in the implicit-barrier construction.

notation.meaning: An admissible parameter assigned to barrier F.
Affine map used for a pullback.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Additive parameter aggregation for products and intersections
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F_i:D_i\to\mathbb R\) be \(\nu_i\)-self-concordant barriers, \(i=1,\ldots,m\), on open convex domains in finite-dimensional spaces. Assume every stated intersection has nonempty interior.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite products and finite intersections of standard self-concordant barriers. The assigned sum is an admissible parameter and need not be the intrinsic optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the Cartesian product \(D=\prod_{i=1}^mD_i\), define the separable barrier \[F_{	imes}(x_1,\ldots,x_m):=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i(x_i).\] For domains \(D_i\subset E\) in a common space, define on \(D_{\cap}= igcap_{i=1}^mD_i\) the intersection barrier \[F_{\cap}(x):=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i(x).\] Product-intersection parameter calculus assigns both barriers the admissible parameter \[
u_{\mathrm{calc}}:=\sum_{i=1}^m
u_i.\] More generally, if constraints are represented by affine maps \(\mathcal A_i:E	o E_i\), then \[D=\{x:\mathcal A_i(x)\in D_i\  orall i\},\qquad F(x)=\sum_iF_i(\mathcal A_i(x))\] inherits the same bound \(\sum_i
u_i\). The block-product rule is the special case in which each \(\mathcal A_i\) is a coordinate projection; the ordinary intersection rule uses identity maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The separable sum of barriers on independent blocks is a barrier for the Cartesian product, and the sum of barriers defined on one space is a barrier for the intersection of their domains. In either case the inherited parameter is the sum of the component parameters. The same formula applies to combined affine constraint representations. This is parameter accounting for a chosen construction, so the resulting sum may be larger than the smallest parameter available for the product or intersection itself.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A product is an intersection of coordinate-pullback domains \(\{x:\pi_i(x)\in D_i\}\).
Combined constraints represented by \(F_i\circ\mathcal A_i\) have aggregate parameter at most \(\sum_i\nu_i\).
special_cases_latex: For \(D=\mathbb R_{++}^m\), summing the one-dimensional barriers \(-\log x_i\) gives parameter \(m\).
For inequalities \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x<b_i\), the sum of the one-dimensional logarithmic barriers has parameter at most the number of inequalities.
immediate_consequences_latex: Adding one represented constraint block increases the calculus parameter by at most that block's parameter.
Block separability makes the Hessian block diagonal, although parameter additivity alone does not quantify the cost of exploiting that structure.
boundary_notes: Nonempty interior is required for the resulting barrier domain.
Parameter additivity is an upper-bound rule; equality requires a separate optimality result.

Parameter supplied by the construction calculus.

children.title: Additive Parameter Accounting

assumptions_latex: For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(F_i\) is a \(\nu_i\)-self-concordant barrier, and all restrictions needed to form \(F:=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i\) are defined on a common nonempty open convex domain.

The finite-sum calculus certifies \(F\) with parameter \(
u(F)\leq
u_{\mathrm{sum}}:=\sum_{i=1}^m
u_i\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite barrier sum \(F:=F_1+\cdots+F_m\), the standard sum calculus gives \(
u(F)\leq
u_{\mathrm{sum}}:=\sum_{i=1}^m
u_i\). This accounting is associative and independent of the order of finite summation. The value \(

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=(0,\infty)\) and \(r\geq1\), summing \(r\) identical logarithmic terms gives \(F_r(x):=-r\log x\). This is a standard self-concordant barrier satisfying \(\|\nabla F_r(x)\|_{x,*}^2=r\), so its certified parameter is \(r\). Thus duplicate constraint terms can raise the certificate from \(1\) to \(r\) without changing \(K\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parameter preservation under affine pullback and restriction
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(E,E_1\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(D\subset E_1\) be open and convex, and let \(F:D\to\mathbb R\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier. Let \(\mathcal A(x)=Ax+b\) be affine.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine preimages and affine slices having nonempty relative interior. The result supplies an inherited parameter; degeneracy can prevent the pullback Hessian from being positive definite on an unreduced ambient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The affine pullback domain and barrier are \[D_{\mathcal A}:=\{x\in E:\mathcal A(x)\in D\},\qquad F_{\mathcal A}(x):=F(\mathcal A(x)).\] Affine pullback-slice calculus assigns \(F_{\mathcal A}\) the same admissible parameter \(
u\), because for every \(x\in D_{\mathcal A}\) and \(h\in E\), \[\langle
abla F_{\mathcal A}(x),hangle=\langle
abla F(\mathcal A x),Ahangle,\quad \langle
abla^2F_{\mathcal A}(x)h,hangle=\langle
abla^2F(\mathcal A x)Ah,Ahangle.\] If \(L=x_0+V\) is an affine subspace meeting \(D\), choose an affine parametrization \(\iota:V	o L\). The restriction \(F|_{D\cap L}\), represented as \(F\circ\iota\) on \(\iota^{-1}(D)\), therefore inherits parameter at most \(
u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composing a ν-self-concordant barrier with an affine map produces a barrier on the affine preimage and does not increase the inherited parameter. Restricting a barrier to an affine slice is the same construction applied to an affine parametrization of that slice. The local metric is pulled back through the linear part of the map, so both the directional derivative and Hessian quadratic form are tested on the image direction Ah.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an inclusion \(\iota:L\hookrightarrow E_1\), affine restriction is the pullback \(F\circ\iota\).
An equality-constrained feasible set \(D\cap\{x:Bx=d\}\) uses the restriction of \(F\) to the affine solution space.
special_cases_latex: Restricting \(-\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i\) to \(\{x:Bx=d\}\cap\mathbb R_{++}^n\) retains the admissible parameter \(n\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Invertible affine changes of coordinates preserve the minimal parameter exactly, by applying the rule in both directions.
An affine formulation can inherit a parameter determined by its lifted or cone domain even when the slice itself admits a smaller barrier.
boundary_notes: When \(A\) has a nontrivial nullspace, the pullback Hessian is singular along that nullspace; a reduced affine parametrization removes redundant directions.
The rule does not state that the inherited value is optimal for the preimage or slice.

notation.meaning: Affine preimage of the barrier domain.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, open, and convex, and \(F:K\to\mathbb{R}\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier.
\(A:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is injective, \(b\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(D:=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^p:Ay+b\in K\}\) is nonempty.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical positive-definite formulation, with injectivity excluding null directions in the pullback Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D:=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^p:Ay+b\in K\}\) be nonempty, where \(A:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is injective. Then the affine pullback \(G(y):=F(Ay+b)\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(D\). Thus an injective affine pullback does not increase the certified parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pulling a barrier back through an injective affine map preserves its certified parameter as an upper bound.

children.title: Affine-Slice Parameters
children.top_down_role: Barrier-parameter behavior under restriction to affine slices.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, open, and convex, and \(F:K\to\mathbb{R}\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier.
\(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(U:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is injective, and \(D:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^p:x_0+Uz\in K\}\) is nonempty.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restriction to a nonempty affine slice expressed in injective reduced coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L:=x_0+\operatorname{range}(U)\) and \(D:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^p:x_0+Uz\in K\}\), where \(U\) is injective and \(D\neq\varnothing\). Then \(G(z):=F(x_0+Uz)\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(D\). Accordingly, restriction to an affine slice does not increase the certified parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expressing a nonempty affine slice in injective coordinates preserves the original barrier parameter as an upper bound.

children.title: Rank-Deficient Pullback Regimes
children.top_down_role: Parameter interpretation when the affine map introduces null directions.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, open, and convex, and \(F:K\to\mathbb{R}\) is a self-concordant barrier with positive-definite Hessian.
\(A:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}^n\) has a nontrivial kernel, \(b\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(D:=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^p:Ay+b\in K\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pullback \(G(y):=F(Ay+b)\) has singular Hessian on \(D\) and is not a classical self-concordant barrier on the full space \(\mathbb{R}^p\); null directions must first be removed.

notation.meaning: Null directions of the linear map.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the classical positive-definite barrier definition under a rank-deficient parameterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(\ker A
eq\{0\}\), then the pullback \(G(y):=F(Ay+b)\) has Hessian \(
abla^2G(y)=A^{\mathsf T}
abla^2F(Ay+b)A\), which is singular on \(D\). Hence \(G\) is not a classical self-concordant barrier on the full parameter space. A quotient construction or complementary reduced coordinates are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-deficient affine pullback has a singular Hessian and becomes a classical barrier only after its null directions are removed.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Pullback Regimes

children.title: Reduced-Space Parameter Preservation
children.top_down_role: Parameter behavior after passing to an effective affine or quotient space.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, open, and convex, and \(F:K\to\mathbb{R}\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier.

notation.meaning: Direct-sum reduction removing exactly the null directions of A.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Removal of precisely the affine-map null directions before applying injective affine invariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q:=\operatorname{rank}A\geq1\) and choose \(U:\mathbb{R}^q\to\mathbb{R}^p\) such that \(\mathbb{R}^p=\ker A\oplus\operatorname{range}(U)\). On \(D:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^q:A(y_0+Uz)+b\in K\}\), the reduced pullback \(H(z):=F(A(y_0+Uz)+b)\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier. Removing the null coordinates therefore does not increase the certified parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choosing coordinates complementary to the affine map's kernel restores a nondegenerate pullback with the original parameter bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Space Parameter Preservation

children.title: Lifted-Representation Parameters
children.top_down_role: Parameter accounting for epigraphs, perspectives, and extended formulations.

assumptions_latex: \(L\subset\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) is open and convex, and \(G:L\to\mathbb{R}\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier.
For every \(x\) in \(K=\operatorname{proj}_xL\), the minimizer \(z(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z:(x,z)\in L}G(x,z)\) exists uniquely.
The marginal Hessian is positive definite on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(F(x)=\inf_{z:(x,z)\in L}G(x,z)
\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier for the projected domain \(K\).

notation.meaning: Lifted feasible set and its projection.
Barrier obtained by eliminating lifted variables.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth partial minimization of a lifted barrier; epigraph and perspective formulations require verifying the stated attainment conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=
\operatorname{proj}_xL\) and define the marginal \(F(x)=
\inf\{G(x,z):(x,z)\in L\}\). Under unique interior attainment and the stated nondegeneracy, differentiation through the minimizer gives the Schur-complement Hessian of \(G\). The self-concordance and barrier-gradient inequalities then pass to the marginal without increasing \(\nu\), so \(F\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier for \(K\). If the lifted barrier is assembled from independent factors, their parameters are first added; that aggregate parameter is therefore inherited as an upper bound after projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regular lifted barrier can be minimized over auxiliary variables to obtain a barrier for the projection without increasing the lift's aggregate parameter.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parameter accounting for epigraph and auxiliary-variable lifts
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on an open convex domain \(D\subset E\). Separately, let \(\Phi\) be a \(\mu\)-self-concordant barrier on an open convex lifted domain \(\widehat D\subset E\times Y\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard epigraph lifting and implicit barriers obtained by uniquely attained partial minimization. General perspectives or arbitrary projections require separate hypotheses and are not included automatically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the epigraph lift \[\operatorname{epi}^{\circ}f:=\{(x,s)\in D\times\mathbb R:s>f(x)\},\] the standard lifted barrier is \[F_{\mathrm{epi}}(x,s):=f(x)-\log(s-f(x)),\] and its calculus parameter is \(\nu+1\). For an auxiliary-variable representation whose projected domain is \[D_{\mathrm{proj}}:=\{x:\exists y\text{ with }(x,y)\in\widehat D\},\] suppose that for every \(x\in D_{\mathrm{proj}}\), the minimizer \(y(x)=\arg\min_y\Phi(x,y)\) exists and is unique. The implicit barrier \[F_{\mathrm{proj}}(x):=\min_y\Phi(x,y)\] inherits parameter \(\mu\). A lifted-representation parameter is the admissible parameter assigned to the barrier on the lifted space before elimination, together with the parameter inherited by the projected implicit barrier after admissible elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard epigraph of a ν-self-concordant barrier has a barrier obtained by adding a logarithmic slack term, and this construction increases the parameter by one. For a more general lifted domain with auxiliary variables, partial minimization of its barrier preserves the parameter when the minimizing auxiliary variable exists uniquely at every projected point. These rules distinguish parameter accounting in the lifted representation from the parameter of the resulting projected barrier.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The epigraph slack \(r=s-f(x)>0\) contributes the one-dimensional logarithmic-barrier parameter \(1\).
The implicit barrier is the value function of the lifted barrier over each projection fiber.
special_cases_latex: Repeated standard epigraph lifts give the calculus bound \(\nu+k\) after \(k\) lifts.
If no auxiliary variables are present, partial minimization is vacuous and the parameter remains \(\mu\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Projection through an implicit-barrier construction need not add to the lifted parameter.
A compact extended formulation can improve structural evaluation costs while carrying a parameter inherited from the lifted domain.
boundary_notes: An arbitrary projection does not by itself define a computable implicit barrier; attainment, uniqueness, and regularity are material.
Perspective constructions are not covered unless realized by a supported affine, epigraph, or implicit-barrier operation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower, universal, and structure-sensitive parameter bounds
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a closed convex set \(Q\subset\mathbb R^n\) with nonempty interior and no lines, let \(\mathcal B(Q)\) denote its standard self-concordant barriers, and define the intrinsic optimal parameter \(\nu_*(Q)=\inf_{F\in\mathcal B(Q)}\nu(F)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional full-dimensional convex domains. The classification concerns mathematical parameter bounds and separates them from computability of the corresponding barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A barrier-parameter bound family is an inequality for \(
u_*(Q)\) or for the parameter of an explicit barrier, classified by the information used. A lower-bound family has the form \[L(Q)\le
u_*(Q),\] where \(L(Q)\) follows from intrinsic geometry such as recession directions or a canonical cone. A universal upper-bound family has the form \[
u_*(Q)\le U(n)\] for every admissible \(Q\subset\mathbb R^n\), independent of an explicit representation. A structure-sensitive family provides a computable barrier \(F_{\mathcal R}\) from representation data \(\mathcal R\) and an estimate \[
u_*(Q)\le
u(F_{\mathcal R})\le S(\mathcal R).\] The three inequalities answer different questions: impossibility of too small a parameter, existence based only on dimension, and attainable quality from specified algebraic structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Barrier-parameter bounds fall into three distinct families. Intrinsic lower bounds limit the smallest parameter any barrier on the domain can have. Universal upper bounds guarantee the existence of a parameter controlled only by ambient dimension. Structure-sensitive bounds attach an explicit, preferably computable barrier and parameter to representation data such as inequalities, cone blocks, or spectral structure. These bounds need not coincide, and only the third automatically supplies an explicit barrier oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The canonical comparison is \[L(Q)\le\nu_*(Q)\le\min\{U(n),\ S(\mathcal R)\},\] whenever the representation-specific construction \(\mathcal R\) is available.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The gap \(S(\mathcal R)-\nu_*(Q)\) measures parameter loss attributable to the selected construction.
Taking a supremum over all \(n\)-dimensional domains converts universal existence bounds into bounds on a worst-case optimal parameter.
special_cases_latex: For \(Q=\mathbb R_+^n\), the logarithmic barrier and the lower bound both give \(\nu_*(Q)=n\).
The universal barrier yields an upper bound \(U(n)=c n\) for an absolute constant \(c\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A universal existence result can be optimal in dimension order while being unsuitable computationally.
An explicit structural barrier can beat a coarse universal constant without attaining \(\nu_*(Q)\).
boundary_notes: Bounds for a particular represented barrier must not be confused with lower bounds applying to every barrier on the domain.
Dimension may refer to the effective affine hull rather than a redundant ambient representation.

notation.meaning: Infimum of admissible parameters over barriers on Q.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-Derivative Bounds for a Univariate Self-Concordant Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided curvature bounds from the base point zero, with the upper bound restricted to the local-metric radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\operatorname{dom}f\subseteq\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) be strictly convex and self-concordant. Then \[\left|\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(f''(t)^{-1/2}\bigr)\right|\le1\qquad(t\in\operatorname{dom}f).\] If \(t\ge0\) and \([0,t]\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\), then \[\frac{f''(0)}{\bigl(1+t\sqrt{f''(0)}\bigr)^2}\le f''(t).\] Moreover, if \(0\le t<f''(0)^{-1/2}\), then \[f''(t)\le\frac{f''(0)}{\bigl(1-t\sqrt{f''(0)}\bigr)^2}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a strictly convex self-concordant function of one variable, the reciprocal square root of the second derivative is 1-Lipschitz. Along a nonnegative interval starting at zero, this gives a global lower bound on the second derivative and an upper bound up to distance one over the square root of the initial second derivative.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\) be a closed convex set with nonempty interior and let \(\nu_*(Q)\) be the infimum of parameters of standard self-concordant barriers on \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The strongest displayed dimension lower bound is for the canonical orthant and positive-semidefinite cones. A linear-in-dimension bound is not asserted for every convex body.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A dimension-dependent lower bound is an inequality \(
u_*(Q_n)\ge L(n)\) for a dimension-indexed domain family \(Q_n\), applying to every self-concordant barrier on each member. Canonical examples are \[
u_*(\mathbb R_+^n)\ge n\] and \[
u_*(\mathbb S_+^n)\ge n,\] where the second \(n\) is matrix order rather than the vector-space dimension \(n(n+1)/2\). These lower bounds are attained by \(-\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i\) and \(-\log\det X\), respectively. More generally every nontrivial barrier domain satisfies \(
u_*(Q)\ge1\), and recession-direction configurations can give additive lower bounds \[
u_*(Q)\ge\sum_{i=1}^k\alpha_i/ eta_i\] under the corresponding geometric hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dimension-dependent lower bound states that every self-concordant barrier on a specified n-indexed family must have parameter at least a function of n. For the nonnegative orthant, every barrier has parameter at least n, and the standard logarithmic barrier attains n. The same statement holds for the positive-semidefinite cone with n denoting matrix order. Such linear bounds are properties of these domain families, not universal lower bounds for all n-dimensional convex sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[
u_*(\mathbb R_+^n)=n,\qquad 
u_*(\mathbb S_+^n)=n,\qquad 
u_*(Q)\ge1\ 	ext{for every nontrivial barrier domain }Q.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: No self-concordant barrier for \(\mathbb R_+^n\) or \(\mathbb S_+^n\) can have admissible parameter strictly below \(n\).
special_cases_latex: For an interval, the one-dimensional lower bound is \(1\).
An affine slice of \(\mathbb R_+^n\) may have a smaller intrinsic lower bound than the full orthant.
immediate_consequences_latex: The standard logarithmic barriers on the orthant and semidefinite cone are parameter-optimal.
Worst-case universal parameter bounds cannot have order smaller than linear in \(n\), because the orthant is an \(n\)-dimensional example.
boundary_notes: The semidefinite lower bound scales with cone rank or matrix order, not ambient vector-space dimension.
Restriction to an affine subspace can reduce the intrinsic optimum even though the inherited barrier retains its original parameter.

u\)-self-concordant barriers on \(K\), then \[

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dimension-only universal barrier bound
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\subset\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex with nonempty interior and containing no affine line. For \(x\in\operatorname{int}Q\), define the polar body based at \(x\) by \[P_Q(x)=\{s\in\mathbb R^n:\langle s,y-x\rangle\le1\ \forall y\in Q\}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence theory for full-dimensional line-free convex sets. The construction is universal but is not claimed to provide an efficiently evaluable oracle for an arbitrary input set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function \(U:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R_+\) is a universal barrier-parameter upper bound if every admissible \(Q\subset\mathbb R^n\) possesses a self-concordant barrier with parameter at most \(U(n)\). The universal-barrier construction sets \[V_Q(x)=\operatorname{vol}_nP_Q(x),\qquad F_Q(x)=c_1\log V_Q(x),\] for an absolute normalization constant \(c_1>0\). There are absolute constants \(c_1,c_2>0\) such that \(F_Q\) is a \(c_2n\)-self-concordant barrier. Consequently \[\nu_*(Q)\le c_2n\] for every such \(Q\), so \(U(n)=c_2n\) is a dimension-controlled universal upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A universal upper bound depends only on dimension and guarantees a barrier for every full-dimensional convex set containing no line. The universal barrier is defined from the volume of the polar body centered at the evaluation point. With absolute normalization constants, it has parameter at most a constant times n. This is an existence statement; evaluating the polar volume and its derivatives may be computationally difficult.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall Q\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ closed, convex, full-dimensional, and line-free},\qquad \nu_*(Q)\le c_2n.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The worst-case optimal parameter \(\sup_Q\nu_*(Q)\) over admissible \(n\)-dimensional domains is \(O(n)\).
special_cases_latex: For a bounded convex body, the line-free condition is automatic.
For the orthant, an explicit logarithmic barrier achieves \(n\), avoiding the generally noncomputable polar-volume construction.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every admissible finite-dimensional convex domain has a self-concordant barrier with parameter linear in dimension.
The associated idealized path-following iteration scale is \(O(\sqrt n\log(n/\epsilon))\), apart from initialization factors.
boundary_notes: The theorem does not make the universal barrier efficiently computable from a generic membership oracle.
Sets containing lines should first be reduced to an effective line-free quotient or affine representation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_i^{\mathsf T}x<b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) be nonempty and contain no affine line. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representation-sensitive bounds from explicit cone and block structure
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a convex domain \(Q\) be given through representation data \(\mathcal R\), such as scalar inequalities, Cartesian cone blocks, affine slices, or a positive-semidefinite matrix variable. Let \(F_{\mathcal R}\) be the barrier produced by the applicable calculus rules.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit finite-dimensional polyhedral, conic, spectral, and separable representations supported by standard logarithmic barriers and parameter calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A structure-sensitive parameter bound is an estimate \[
u(F_{\mathcal R})\le S(\mathcal R)\] whose right-hand side depends on algebraic representation data rather than only on ambient dimension. Canonical instances include \[F(x)=-\sum_{i=1}^m\log(b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x),\qquad 
u(F)\le m,\] for \(m\) strict affine inequalities; \[F(X)=-\log\det X,\qquad 
u(F)=r,\] on \(\mathbb S_{++}^r\); and additive aggregation \[S(\mathcal R)=\sum_{j=1}^k
u_j\] for products or intersections of blocks with parameters \(
u_j\). Affine restriction preserves the inherited bound. Such a bound may be much smaller than one based on the vector-space dimension of a lifted matrix representation, but it remains tied to the selected formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structure-sensitive bound uses explicit features of the formulation. A polyhedron represented by m inequalities has the standard logarithmic barrier bound m. A positive-semidefinite cone of matrix order r has the log-determinant parameter r, despite having vector-space dimension r(r+1)/2. Product and combined-constraint parameters add across blocks, while affine slicing does not increase the inherited value. The result is a bound for the represented barrier and may differ across equivalent formulations of the same projected feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For supported representation blocks, \[\nu(F_{\mathcal R})\le S(\mathcal R)=\sum_j\nu_j,\] with scalar logarithmic inequalities contributing \(1\) each and an \(r\times r\) semidefinite block contributing \(r\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a block-diagonal semidefinite cone with block orders \(r_j\), the separable log-determinant barrier has parameter \(\sum_jr_j\).
A polyhedral logarithmic barrier is the sum of pullbacks of one-dimensional ray barriers.
special_cases_latex: The orthant \(\mathbb R_+^n\) has the structure-sensitive and optimal value \(n\).
The Lorentz-cone logarithmic barrier has parameter \(2\), independent of the cone's vector-space dimension.
immediate_consequences_latex: Exploiting block structure can improve both parameter accounting and Newton-system structure.
Redundant represented inequalities can enlarge the calculus parameter without changing the feasible set.
boundary_notes: The number of represented constraints is not an intrinsic invariant of the domain.
A smaller structure-sensitive parameter does not alone imply lower arithmetic cost if derivative evaluation or factorization becomes more expensive.

notation.meaning: Parameter bound extracted from that representation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Worst-case optimal universal barrier parameter
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal Q_n\) be the class of closed, full-dimensional, line-free convex subsets of \(\mathbb R^n\). For \(Q\in\mathcal Q_n\), define \(\nu_*(Q)=\inf_F\nu(F)\), where the infimum ranges over standard self-concordant barriers on \(\operatorname{int}Q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal order of the worst-case universal parameter in finite dimension. The record does not claim a sharp leading constant or efficient evaluation of an optimal barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the worst-case intrinsic universal parameter by \[\mathfrak U(n):=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal Q_n}\nu_*(Q).\] An optimal-order universal-parameter result consists of matching dimension-order bounds on \(\mathfrak U(n)\). The orthant gives \[\mathfrak U(n)\ge\nu_*(\mathbb R_+^n)=n,\] while the universal-barrier construction gives an absolute constant \(c_2\) such that \[\mathfrak U(n)\le c_2n.\] Therefore \[\mathfrak U(n)=\Theta(n).\] This means that linear dependence on dimension is simultaneously sufficient for every admissible domain and necessary in the worst case. It does not imply that each individual domain has optimal parameter proportional to its ambient dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The worst-case intrinsic universal parameter is the supremum, over all full-dimensional line-free convex domains in dimension n, of the smallest barrier parameter available on that domain. The nonnegative orthant forces this quantity to be at least n. The universal barrier bounds it above by an absolute constant times n. Hence the optimal worst-case order is linear in dimension, although particular domains or affine slices can have smaller intrinsic parameters.
equivalent_formulations_latex: There exist absolute constants \(a,b>0\) such that \(an\le\mathfrak U(n)\le bn\) for every \(n\ge1\).
No universal guarantee \(o(n)\) can hold over all \(n\)-dimensional domains, while an \(O(n)\) guarantee does hold.
special_cases_latex: The orthant attains the lower comparison \(\nu_*(\mathbb R_+^n)=n\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The worst-case short-step iteration factor derived solely from universal barrier existence has optimal dimension order \(\sqrt n\), up to constants and logarithmic terms.
Improving the universal-barrier constant does not change the linear parameter order.
boundary_notes: This is an order-optimal result, not a sharp-constant characterization.
The supplied evidence establishes the classical \(\Theta(n)\) conclusion; it does not support a stronger modern asymptotic constant.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Joint parameter and oracle quality of a barrier representation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\) be a convex feasible set and let \(\mathfrak R(Q)\) be a class of barrier representations. Each \(R\in\mathfrak R(Q)\) supplies a barrier \(F_R\), an admissible parameter \(\nu_R\), and a per-iteration oracle or Newton-system cost \(C_R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic comparison model for exact short-step methods. The cost component must be fixed for the computational model being compared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every barrier representation has at least two relevant quality coordinates: its admissible parameter and the cost of using its derivative oracle and Newton system. One representation dominates another only if it is no worse in both coordinates. For short-step methods, a natural total-work proxy multiplies per-iteration cost by the square root of the parameter and a logarithmic accuracy factor. The best parameter alone need not select the least expensive formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The representation choice is evaluated through \[\min_{R\in\mathfrak R(Q)}C_R\sqrt{\nu_R}\log(S_R/\epsilon),\] or through the Pareto frontier of \((\nu_R,C_R)\) when no single cost model is fixed.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Iteration complexity and arithmetic complexity are separate coordinates of barrier quality.
A representation with larger \(\nu_R\) can have smaller total work if it sufficiently reduces \(C_R\).
special_cases_latex: A universal barrier has \(\nu_R=O(n)\) but may have prohibitive polar-volume oracle cost.
An explicit logarithmic barrier can have a larger representation parameter yet inexpensive structured derivatives.
immediate_consequences_latex: Parameter-optimal and runtime-optimal representations need not coincide.
Redundant lifting can worsen \(\nu_R\) while improving sparsity or factorization structure, producing an actual tradeoff.
boundary_notes: The cost proxy omits constants, numerical conditioning, and inexact-solve effects unless included in \(C_R\).
Comparisons require a common accuracy criterion and computational model.
