knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton recentering for a self-concordant path objective
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(F:\operatorname{dom}F\to\mathbb R\) be a self-concordant barrier with positive-definite Hessian on the open convex set \(\operatorname{dom}F\), and let \(c\in E^*\). For \(t\geq0\), set \(f_t(x)=t\langle c,x\rangle+F(x)\), \(\|u\|_x=\langle\nabla^2F(x)u,u\rangle^{1/2}\), and \(\|v\|_x^*=\langle v,[\nabla^2F(x)]^{-1}v\rangle^{1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, smooth, exact-arithmetic recentering for the primal barrier path; the definition does not cover primal-dual scaling directions or inexact linear solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a target parameter \(t_+\geq0\) and \(x\in\operatorname{dom}F\), define the target Newton residual and decrement by \(r_{t_+}(x)=t_+c+
abla F(x)\) and \(\lambda_{t_+}(x)=\|r_{t_+}(x)\|_x^*\). The Newton recentering map is \(R_{t_+}(x)=x-[
abla^2F(x)]^{-1}r_{t_+}(x)\); a damped recentering with damping \(a\in(0,1]\) is \(R_{t_+,a}(x)=x-a[
abla^2F(x)]^{-1}r_{t_+}(x)\). Relative to a prescribed centrality radius \( eta\in(0,1)\), the update is a successful Newton recentering when \(R_{t_+,a}(x)\in\operatorname{dom}F\) and \(\lambda_{t_+}(R_{t_+,a}(x))\leq eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the barrier objective at a new path parameter, Newton recentering evaluates its gradient residual in the local Hessian metric and subtracts the inverse-Hessian residual, possibly with damping. Relative to a fixed centrality radius, the recentering is successful exactly when the updated point remains in the barrier domain and its Newton decrement for the new objective is at most that radius.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is twice differentiable on \(\operatorname{dom}F\) and \(\nabla^2F(x)\succ0\) at the point being updated.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The undamped correction \(\Delta x=-[\nabla^2F(x)]^{-1}r_{t_+}(x)\) is the unique solution of \(\nabla^2F(x)\Delta x=-r_{t_+}(x)\).
Exact centrality at the target parameter is \(r_{t_+}(x)=0\), equivalently \(\lambda_{t_+}(x)=0\).
special_cases_latex: For \(a=1\), \(R_{t_+,1}\) is the full Newton recentering map.
If \(t_+=t\), the update improves centering for the current path objective rather than compensating for a parameter change.
immediate_consequences_latex: A successful recentering returns the iterate to the certified neighborhood \(\mathcal N_\beta(t_+)=\{y\in\operatorname{dom}F:\lambda_{t_+}(y)\leq\beta\}\).
The recentering map is defined only where the local Hessian is invertible.
boundary_notes: The definition itself does not assert that a proposed parameter change or damping factor makes recentering successful.
Approximate Newton systems require a separate residual-error condition.

notation.meaning: Damped Newton recentering map for the target parameter.
Newton decrement of the barrier objective \(f_t\) at \(x\).

A proposed starting point \(x_0\) lies in \(Q=\operatorname{dom}F\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\lambda_{t_0}(x_0)=\|t_0c+\nabla F(x_0)\|_{x_0,*}\). The pair \((x_0,t_0)\) is a certified initial center at radius \(\beta\) when \[x_0\in\operatorname{dom}F\quad\text{and}\quad\lambda_{t_0}(x_0)\leq\beta<1.\] This condition permits the cited local parameter-change and Newton-recentering estimates to be applied from the first path-following iteration; without such a certificate, those local estimates provide no initialization guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Path tracking starts in its certified local regime when the initial point is interior and its barrier-subproblem Newton decrement is below the chosen threshold.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified initial-center interface
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(\operatorname{dom}F\subset E\), let \(f_t(x)=t\langle c,x\rangle+F(x)\), and define \(\lambda_t(x)=\|tc+\nabla F(x)\|_x^*\). Fix a centrality radius \(\beta\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional primal short-step path following. This interface separates initialization from the subsequent certified tracking phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A certified initial-center interface is a tuple \(I_0=(t_0,x_0,\beta,C_0)\) such that \(t_0\geq0\), \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}F\), \(\lambda_{t_0}(x_0)\leq\beta\), and \(C_0\in\mathbb N\cup\{0\}\) is a certified upper bound on the computational work used to produce \(x_0\) from the supplied problem data. A path-following complexity statement accepts this interface only when its tracking hypotheses begin at every pair \((t_0,x_0)\) satisfying the displayed membership and centrality conditions; initialization work is accounted for separately as \(C_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The initial-center interface consists of a starting path parameter, an interior point whose Newton decrement is within the prescribed central neighborhood, and a certified bound on the work needed to construct that point. The tracking phase may use the point only after these conditions are verified, and its iteration bound does not silently absorb an unspecified initialization procedure.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier and its local dual norm is computable at \(x_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[I_0\ \text{is certified}\iff t_0\geq0,\quad x_0\in\operatorname{dom}F,\quad \|t_0c+\nabla F(x_0)\|_{x_0}^*\leq\beta,\quad C_0\ \text{bounds initialization work}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(t_0=0\), certification is \(\|\nabla F(x_0)\|_{x_0}^*\leq\beta\), so \(x_0\) is an approximate analytic center.
Writing \(\mathcal N_\beta(t)=\{x\in\operatorname{dom}F:\lambda_t(x)\leq\beta\}\), the centrality condition is \(x_0\in\mathcal N_\beta(t_0)\).
special_cases_latex: An exact analytic center gives \(t_0=0\) and \(\lambda_0(x_0)=0\).
If the problem input directly supplies a verified center, one may take \(C_0=0\) in an iteration-only accounting convention.
immediate_consequences_latex: A tracking bound starting from \(I_0\) is conditional unless \(C_0\) is itself bounded in the chosen computational model.
Failure of either domain membership or the decrement test prevents invocation of the short-step tracking guarantee.
boundary_notes: A merely feasible point need not be a certified center.
The interface does not prescribe a unique phase-I construction; auxiliary-path and embedding methods are separate implementations.

notation.meaning: Certified work bound for constructing the initial center.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Self-concordant path-following complexity theorem family
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider finite-dimensional convex programs represented by a linear objective over a convex domain possessing a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier. Let \(\epsilon>0\) denote a requested objective-gap or primal-dual-gap accuracy, and let \(\beta\in(0,1)\) denote a certified central-neighborhood radius.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is a definition of the common theorem template, not an assertion that every convex program or implementation satisfies it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The self-concordant path-following complexity theorem family is the collection of results indexed by a problem representation \(P\), barrier parameter \(
u\), neighborhood radius \( eta\), initialization certificate \(I_0\), correction model \(\mathfrak C\), and accuracy certificate \(\mathfrak A\), whose hypotheses guarantee: every generated iterate remains in the declared interior neighborhood; the path parameter changes by a relative amount of order \(
u^{-1/2}\) per bounded number of corrections; and an \(\epsilon\)-certificate is obtained after \(K\leq C\sqrt
u\log(M/\epsilon)+K_0\) corrections. Here \(C\) is independent of \(
u\) and \(\epsilon\), \(M>0\) is the theorem's stated initial scale, and \(K_0\) is its separately stated initialization contribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This theorem family consists of path-following results whose data explicitly identify the barrier quality, central neighborhood, starting certificate, correction accuracy, and stopping certificate. A member guarantees neighborhood invariance and reaches the requested accuracy in a number of Newton-type corrections proportional to the square root of the barrier parameter times a logarithmic accuracy factor, plus any separately quantified initialization cost.
assumptions_latex: The problem representation supplies a computable \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on a nonempty interior domain.
The initial-center certificate \(I_0\), correction model \(\mathfrak C\), and accuracy certificate \(\mathfrak A\) satisfy the particular member theorem's explicit hypotheses.
The scale \(M\) and initialization contribution \(K_0\) are finite and specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[K(P,\epsilon)\leq C\sqrt\nu\log(M/\epsilon)+K_0,\quad x_k\in\mathcal N_\beta(t_k)\ \text{for all generated iterates},\quad \mathfrak A(x_K)\leq\epsilon.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A constant-factor increase in the path parameter costs \(O(\sqrt\nu)\) corrections, while a reduction of the accuracy scale from \(M\) to \(\epsilon\) requires \(O(\log(M/\epsilon))\) such factors.
special_cases_latex: For linear programming with the standard logarithmic barrier, \(\nu\) is proportional to the number of inequality or cone coordinates.
For an exact short-step method with a certified initial center, \(K_0=0\) under tracking-only iteration accounting.
immediate_consequences_latex: The family organizes distinct theorems by their initialization, neighborhood, and correction hypotheses rather than treating all interior-point variants as interchangeable.
The displayed correction count alone does not determine arithmetic or bit complexity.
boundary_notes: The constant \(C\), scale \(M\), certificate, and admissible correction errors depend on the selected member theorem.
Long-step, infeasible-start, and predictor-corrector results belong only when separately instantiated with their own hypotheses.

notation.meaning: Exact or inexact correction model specified by a member theorem.
Accuracy certificate controlled by a member theorem.

children.title: Short-Step Path-Following Complexity
children.top_down_role: Canonical narrow-neighborhood complexity governed by the barrier parameter.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and convex, \(F:Q\to\mathbb{R}\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier, and the original objective is linear.
A certified pair \((x_0,t_0)\), with \(t_0>0\), lies in a fixed narrow Newton-decrement neighborhood \(\lambda_{t_0}(x_0)\leq\beta\), where \(\beta\in(0,1)\).

For fixed admissible constants \(\sigma>0\) and \(C_\beta>0\), each iteration replaces \(t\) by \((1+\sigma/\sqrt{\nu})t\), performs one full Newton step, preserves \(\lambda_t(x)\leq\beta\), and satisfies the objective certificate \(\langle c,x\rangle-p_*\leq C_\beta\nu/t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Objective error at most \(\varepsilon>0\) is reached in \(O\!\left(\sqrt{\nu}\log_+\!\left(C_\beta\nu/(t_0\varepsilon)\right)\right)\) exact Newton steps.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical exact-Newton short-step bound for a linear objective and fixed narrow neighborhood.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Canonical short-step path-following complexity
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For the primal-dual linear program, let \(\mathcal F^o\) be the strictly feasible set, \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\), \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), \(e=(1,\ldots,1)\), and \(\mu=x^Ts/n\). Define \(\mathcal N_2(\theta)=\{(x,\lambda,s)\in\mathcal F^o:\|XSe-\mu e\|_2\leq\theta\mu\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic feasible-start primal-dual short-step method for linear programming, using the specific constants in Wright's Algorithm SPF.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Short-step path-following complexity is the correction bound attached to Algorithm SPF: start from \((x^0,\lambda^0,s^0)\in\mathcal N_2(0.4)\), choose \(\sigma=1-0.4/\sqrt n\), solve the primal-dual Newton equations exactly, and take the full step at every iteration. The iterates remain in \(\mathcal N_2(0.4)\), and \(\mu_{k+1}=\sigma\mu_k\). Consequently, if \(\mu_0\leq\epsilon^{-\kappa}\) for a constant \(\kappa>0\), the short-step correction complexity is \(K(\epsilon)=O(\sqrt n\log(1/\epsilon))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The canonical linear-programming short-step complexity applies to a strictly feasible point in the narrow two-norm neighborhood. Each iteration solves the exact primal-dual Newton equations, takes a unit step, and uses a centering factor equal to one minus 0.4 divided by the square root of the dimension. The neighborhood is invariant, the duality measure contracts by that factor, and the requested duality tolerance is reached in order square-root-of-dimension times logarithmic-in-accuracy iterations.
assumptions_latex: The Newton system is solved exactly and the full step is taken.
\(\epsilon>0\) and the linear program admits the stated strictly feasible primal-dual start.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A constant-factor reduction of \(\mu\) requires \(O(\sqrt n)\) full Newton corrections.
special_cases_latex: For a general logarithmic-barrier representation, the dimension factor is replaced by the square root of the corresponding barrier parameter when supported by the appropriate self-concordant theorem.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every iterate remains strictly primal-dual feasible.
The bound is an iteration count and does not include the cost of producing the initial point or solving each Newton system.
boundary_notes: The definition does not cover the wider one-sided neighborhood used by long-step methods.
Changing the neighborhood, centering constant, or solve accuracy requires a different invariant-neighborhood result.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Short-step path-following complexity for convex QCQP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton-iteration complexity for a strictly feasible convex QCQP in epigraph form using its logarithmic barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\tau\in\mathbb{R}}\tau subject to q_0(x)\le\tau and q_i(x)\le\beta_i for i=1,\ldots,m, where q_i(x)=\alpha_i+\langle a_i,x\rangle+\tfrac12\langle A_i x,x\rangle and A_i\succeq0 for i=0,\ldots,m. Assume \mathcal D=\{(x,\tau):q_0(x)<\tau,\ q_i(x)<\beta_i\ (i=1,\ldots,m)\}\ne\varnothing, and set F(x,\tau)=-\ln(\tau-q_0(x))-\sum_{i=1}^m\ln(\beta_i-q_i(x)). Then a short-step path-following method for \phi_t(x,\tau)=t\tau+F(x,\tau), t>0, produces a feasible (x,\tau) satisfying \tau-\tau^*\le\epsilon in O\!\left(\sqrt{m+1}\ln\frac{m}{\epsilon}\right) Newton iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a strictly feasible convex QCQP in epigraph form, a short-step path-following method based on the sum-of-log-slacks barrier reaches objective error at most epsilon in order square-root of m plus one times log of m over epsilon Newton iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ a short-step path-following method producing feasible }(x,\tau)\text{ with }\tau-\tau^*\le\epsilon\text{ in }O\!\left(\sqrt{m+1}\ln\frac{m}{\epsilon}\right)\text{ Newton iterations}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Path-following complexity for maximum-volume inscribed ellipsoids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the model-specific path-following guarantee under nonempty-interior and exact barrier-parameter assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume that the feasible set of
\[
\min_{G\in\mathbb{S}_+^n,\,v\in\mathbb{R}^n,\,\tau\in\mathbb{R}}
\left\{\tau:-\ln\det G\le\tau,\ \|Ga_i\|\le b_i-\langle a_i,v\rangle,\ i=1,\ldots,m\right\}
\]
has nonempty interior. Equip it with
\[
F(G,v,\tau)=-\ln\det G-\ln(\tau+\ln\det G)-\sum_{i=1}^m\ln\!\left((b_i-\langle a_i,v\rangle)^2-\|Ga_i\|^2\right),
\]
whose barrier parameter is $\nu=2m+n+1$. Then a path-following interior-point scheme computes an $\varepsilon$-accurate solution in
\[
O\!\left(\sqrt{2m+n+1}\,\ln\frac{m+n}{\varepsilon}\right)
\]
iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the convex maximum-volume inscribed-ellipsoid formulation has nonempty interior, its stated barrier has parameter 2m+n+1, and path following computes an epsilon-accurate solution in order square-root(2m+n+1) times log((m+n)/epsilon) iterations.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Self-concordant path-following Newton-iteration bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the barrier-parameter-controlled path-following bound under the source's central-path neighborhood, constant-factor update, and damped-Newton assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $F(H,\tau)$ be a self-concordant barrier for a convex optimization problem with barrier parameter $\nu\le m+n+1$. Suppose a path-following interior-point method follows the central path, decreases its barrier parameter by a constant factor at each outer iteration, and uses damped Newton steps to maintain a point in a fixed neighborhood of the central path. Then, for every $\epsilon\in(0,1)$, it returns an $\epsilon$-accurate solution in at most
\[
O\!\left(\sqrt{m+n+1}\,\ln\frac{m+n}{\epsilon}\right)
\]
Newton iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated self-concordance, parameter, central-neighborhood, constant-factor update, and damped-Newton assumptions, path following reaches epsilon accuracy in order square-root(m+n+1) times log((m+n)/epsilon) Newton iterations.

\text{Each outer iteration decreases the method's barrier parameter by a constant factor}
\text{Damped Newton steps maintain a point in a fixed central-path neighborhood}

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear convex functional-constraint problem inherits self-concordant path complexity when its basic set and all relevant epigraphs have computable self-concordant barriers. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complexity of reaching the starting neighborhood
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier, let \(\beta\in(0,1)\), and let \(\mathcal N_\beta(t)=\{x\in\operatorname{dom}F:\|tc+\nabla F(x)\|_x^*\leq\beta\}\). Let \(y_0\in\operatorname{dom}F\) be an available interior point that need not be centered.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary-path initialization for a primal self-concordant barrier scheme; it measures the preliminary corrections before ordinary path tracking begins.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The starting-neighborhood complexity \(K_{\mathrm{start}}(y_0,\beta)\) is the least certified number of Newton-type corrections required by the specified initialization procedure to output some \((t_0,x_0)\) with \(x_0\in\mathcal N_\beta(t_0)\). For the auxiliary path joining \(y_0\) to the analytic center, this cost is bounded by a quantity of order \(\sqrt\nu\) times logarithms of \(\nu\) and the declared initial gradient scale. The total correction count is defined additively by \(K_{\mathrm{total}}(\epsilon)=K_{\mathrm{start}}+K_{\mathrm{track}}(\epsilon;t_0,x_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting-neighborhood complexity counts the certified preliminary Newton corrections needed to turn an available interior point into a point satisfying the path method's centrality test. For auxiliary path initialization, its leading dependence is square root of the barrier parameter times logarithms of the barrier and initial gradient scale. This cost is added to, rather than hidden inside, the subsequent tracking cost.
assumptions_latex: An interior point \(y_0\in\operatorname{dom}F\) and the local barrier oracle are available.
The initialization procedure declares a stopping test that guarantees membership in \(\mathcal N_\beta(t_0)\).
All logarithmic scale quantities appearing in its bound are finite.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For analytic-center initialization, the target condition is \(\|\nabla F(x_0)\|_{x_0}^*\leq\beta\).
Initialization complexity is a phase-I correction count with a centrality certificate as its output contract.
special_cases_latex: If the supplied point already lies in \(\mathcal N_\beta(t_0)\), then \(K_{\mathrm{start}}=0\).
If only an arbitrary interior point is known, the auxiliary central path may be traced toward an approximate analytic center.
immediate_consequences_latex: A tracking-only bound is not a complete end-to-end iteration bound unless \(K_{\mathrm{start}}\) is zero or separately controlled.
The starting procedure may have the same \(O(\sqrt\nu)\) leading barrier dependence as the main path-following phase.
boundary_notes: This definition presupposes that at least one usable interior point is available; constructing such a point can require another phase-I procedure.
The minimum is relative to the declared initialization model and oracle, not over all conceivable algorithms.

children.top_down_role: Complexity preservation under controlled approximate centering and linear solves.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier and the initial pair satisfies \(\lambda_{t_0}(x_0)\leq\beta\).
Each approximate correction has local residual at most a fixed \(\eta\), and the chosen constants preserve \(\lambda_{t_k}(x_k)\leq\beta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The number of approximate centering steps needed to reach \(t_k\geq t_f\) is \(O(\sqrt{\nu}\log(t_f/t_0))\).

notation.meaning: Uniform allowed local residual or solve error

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract complexity preservation theorem conditional on a uniform inexactness rule that keeps every iterate central.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose an approximate Newton correction is computed at every iteration with an error bounded by \(\eta\) in the current local norm, and suppose \(\eta\), \(\sigma\), and \(\beta\) are fixed constants for which the inexact update preserves the neighborhood invariant \(\lambda_{t_k}(x_k)\leq\beta\). Since
\[
t_k=t_0\left(1+\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{\nu}}\right)^k,
\]
the first index satisfying \(t_k\geq t_f\) obeys
\[
k=O\!\left(\sqrt{\nu}\log\frac{t_f}{t_0}\right).
\]
Thus controlled approximate centering and linear solves preserve the short-step iteration order; their internal computational cost is not included in this count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly bounded approximate Newton errors preserve the short-step iteration order when every inexact correction maintains the prescribed central-path neighborhood.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complexity preservation under inexact path corrections
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At iteration \(k\), let the exact Newton correction solve \(H_k\Delta_k=-g_k\), where \(H_k\succ0\). Let an implementation return \(\widetilde\Delta_k\) with linear residual \(e_k=H_k\widetilde\Delta_k+g_k\), measured in the dual local norm \(\|e_k\|_{H_k^{-1}}=\langle e_k,H_k^{-1}e_k\rangle^{1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A conditional complexity definition for deterministic inexact Newton corrections. It does not prescribe universal admissible tolerances for every barrier or factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An inexact path-following method is complexity preserving relative to an exact short-step theorem if it specifies tolerances \(\eta_k\geq0\) such that \(\|e_k\|_{H_k^{-1}}\leq\eta_k\), and these tolerances imply both neighborhood invariance and a uniform progress estimate \(q_{k+1}\leq(1-ho/\sqrt
u)q_k\) for some \(ho>0\) independent of \(k,
u\), and the requested accuracy. Its inexact correction complexity is then \(K_{\mathrm{inexact}}(\epsilon)=O(\sqrt
u\log(q_0/\epsilon))\); the arithmetic or bit cost additionally includes the work required to attain every \(\eta_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate-solve path method preserves the short-step complexity when its Newton residual tolerances are strong enough to keep every iterate in the certified neighborhood and retain a uniform square-root-barrier contraction of the progress measure. Under those explicit conditions, the correction count has the same asymptotic form as in the exact method, but the computational cost must also include the work of meeting the solve tolerances.
assumptions_latex: Each approximate correction has a certified local residual bound \(\|e_k\|_{H_k^{-1}}\leq\eta_k\).
The chosen tolerance rule is known to imply neighborhood invariance for the particular barrier and update scheme.
There exists \(\rho>0\), independent of \(k\), \(\nu\), and \(\epsilon\), for which the stated progress inequality holds.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Complexity preservation means that inexactness changes only constants in the certified correction bound, not its \(\sqrt\nu\log(1/\epsilon)\) order.
special_cases_latex: Exact Newton corrections correspond to \(e_k=0\) and \(\eta_k=0\).
Rational rounding schemes are covered only when their rounding error satisfies the declared residual and invariance conditions.
immediate_consequences_latex: A small Euclidean residual alone is insufficient unless related to the local metric used in the analysis.
Correction complexity and the cost of iterative linear algebra are distinct quantities.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validity boundary of abstract path-following complexity
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal T=(\mathcal P,F,\nu,\mathcal N,I_0,\mathfrak C,\mathfrak A,\mathfrak M)\) denote a proposed path-following complexity specification: problem class, barrier, barrier parameter, neighborhood, initialization, correction model, accuracy certificate, and computational model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A formal scope boundary for self-concordant path-following statements; it distinguishes a conditional iteration theorem from an end-to-end computational guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The path-following validity domain \(\operatorname{Dom}_{\mathrm{PF}}\) is the set of specifications \(\mathcal T\) for which: \(F\) is a computable \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier for every represented instance; \(I_0\) supplies a certified point in \(\mathcal N\); every correction allowed by \(\mathfrak C\) preserves domain membership and \(\mathcal N\); \(\mathfrak A\) converts the path parameter or gap into the requested solution accuracy; and the costs charged by \(\mathfrak M\) are explicitly declared. A path-following boundary is any failure of one of these predicates. Outside \(\operatorname{Dom}_{\mathrm{PF}}\), the abstract correction bound is undefined rather than a computational guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The abstract theory applies only when the barrier is computable and self-concordant, initialization reaches the certified neighborhood, allowed corrections preserve that neighborhood and the interior domain, the stopping quantity certifies the requested solution accuracy, and the computational cost model is declared. Failure of any one condition lies beyond the theorem's validity boundary, so a correction count cannot be promoted to an end-to-end algorithmic guarantee.
assumptions_latex: A proposed specification \(\mathcal T\) identifies every listed component.
Each component is interpreted in one fixed finite-dimensional problem and computational model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal T\in\operatorname{Dom}_{\mathrm{PF}}\iff B_{\mathrm{bar}}(\mathcal T)\wedge B_{\mathrm{start}}(\mathcal T)\wedge B_{\mathrm{inv}}(\mathcal T)\wedge B_{\mathrm{cert}}(\mathcal T)\wedge B_{\mathrm{cost}}(\mathcal T);\quad \text{boundary}\iff\text{at least one predicate fails}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The validity domain is the intersection of the barrier, start, invariance, certificate, and cost domains.
A tracking theorem with an unverified start or undeclared per-step cost is a conditional result, not a full complexity theorem.
special_cases_latex: An exact short-step theorem with a supplied analytic center satisfies the start predicate directly.
A real-arithmetic iteration statement may satisfy the tracking predicates while failing to establish bit complexity.
immediate_consequences_latex: Barrier existence alone does not establish computational tractability.
Neighborhood invariance is a necessary interface between local Newton behavior and the global correction count.
boundary_notes: This definition does not assert impossibility outside the domain; it says only that the selected theorem does not apply.
Alternative embeddings, neighborhoods, or algorithm variants may establish a different validity domain.

The point \(x(t)\in\operatorname{int}Q\) minimizes \(\phi_t\), where \(t>0\), and the parameter changes to \(t'>0\) before the point is corrected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(|t'-t|\|c\|_{x(t),*}>\beta\), then \(x(t)\notin\mathcal N_{t'}(\beta)\), and a theorem requiring membership in that neighborhood is inapplicable until centrality is restored.

notation.meaning: Exact central point at parameter t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact parameter-jump mechanism by which an old central point can fail the new neighborhood test.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Optimality of \(x(t)\) gives \(tc+\nabla F(x(t))=0\). Hence, after changing the parameter without changing the point,
\[
\nabla\phi_{t'}(x(t))=(t'-t)c,
\qquad
\lambda_{t'}(x(t))=|t'-t|\,\|c\|_{x(t),*}.
\]
Therefore, if \(|t'-t|\,\|c\|_{x(t),*}>\beta\), then \(x(t)\notin\mathcal N_{t'}(\beta)\). More generally, a corrected iterate whose decrement exceeds \(\beta\) fails the same neighborhood invariant, so conclusions conditional on that invariant cannot be invoked until it is restored.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unchanged central point loses the prescribed centrality after a parameter jump when its new Newton decrement exceeds the neighborhood radius; the same boundary applies to an inaccurate correction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Loss of centrality under a path update
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal N_\beta(t)=\{x\in\operatorname{dom}F:\lambda_t(x)\leq\beta\}\), where \(\lambda_t(x)=\|tc+\nabla F(x)\|_x^*\), and let an update propose a new parameter \(t_+\) and corrected point \(x_+\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal Newton-decrement neighborhood, with a parallel primal-dual interpretation obtained by replacing the decrement neighborhood with the theorem's declared primal-dual neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Loss of centrality occurs at an update \((t,x)\mapsto(t_+,x_+)\) when \((t,x)\) is certified central but the updated pair is not: \(x\in\mathcal N_\beta(t)\) and either \(x_+\notin\operatorname{dom}F\) or \(\lambda_{t_+}(x_+)>\beta\). Parameter-induced loss before correction is the special event \(x\in\mathcal N_\beta(t)\) but \(\lambda_{t_+}(x)>\beta\). Correction-induced loss occurs when the pre-correction target point is admissible but the chosen correction produces \(x_+\notin\mathcal N_\beta(t_+)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Centrality is lost when a previously certified iterate ceases to belong to the prescribed neighborhood after changing the path parameter or applying a correction. The failure includes leaving the barrier domain. One can distinguish loss caused immediately by an overly large parameter change from loss caused by an unsafe, inaccurate, or excessively large correction.
assumptions_latex: The target parameter \(t_+\) and proposed correction \(x_+\) are defined.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(x_+\in\operatorname{dom}F\), loss of centrality is equivalent to \(x_+\notin\mathcal N_\beta(t_+)\).
For a primal-dual neighborhood \(\mathcal N_\beta\), the same event is membership before and nonmembership after the update.
special_cases_latex: With no correction, set \(x_+=x\) to isolate loss caused by changing \(t\).
With \(t_+=t\), the event isolates loss caused by the correction itself.
immediate_consequences_latex: Once loss occurs, an invariant-neighborhood theorem cannot be invoked for the next short-step iteration without a separate recovery argument.
Leaving the barrier domain also makes the local Hessian metric unavailable at the proposed point.
boundary_notes: A larger neighborhood may still contain the updated point; centrality loss is relative to the declared radius and metric.
The definition does not quantify how many recentering steps are required for recovery.

notation.meaning: Predicate that the update leaves the certified neighborhood.

children.title: Missing or Inaccessible Starts
children.top_down_role: Absence of a computable initial central point or normalized analytic center.

assumptions_latex: A path-following theorem for a convex set \(Q\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) and a barrier \(F:\operatorname{int}Q\to\mathbb{R}\) assumes that a pair \((x_0,t_0)\) with \(t_0>0\), \(x_0\in\operatorname{int}Q\), and \(\lambda_{t_0}(x_0)\leq\beta\) is supplied.
The theorem's stated iteration count begins only after this initial pair is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the required initial pair does not exist or cannot be computed in the declared access model, the theorem remains conditional and yields no executable end-to-end complexity bound.

notation.meaning: Required initial interior point and path parameter
Newton decrement at the initial pair

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of a warm-start theorem when its required interior, centered initialization cannot be produced.

source_refs.locator: §4.2.4, “Path-following scheme,” p. 199

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A path-following iteration theorem whose hypotheses require \(x_0\in\operatorname{int}Q\) and \(\lambda_{t_0}(x_0)\leq\beta\) applies only after such a pair \((x_0,t_0)\) has been supplied. If \(\operatorname{int}Q=\varnothing\) in the modeled ambient space, no qualifying \(x_0\) exists. If a qualifying pair exists but cannot be produced under the declared access model, the theorem still gives no executable cold-start method. A reformulation, an explicit certified start, or a separately analyzed Phase-I procedure is then required for an end-to-end complexity guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A warm-start path-following theorem gives no executable end-to-end bound when its required interior, centered initial pair is nonexistent or inaccessible under the computational model.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Missing and computationally inaccessible path starts
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Fix a represented problem instance \(P\), a barrier \(F_P\), a target starting neighborhood \(\mathcal N_\beta(t_0)\), a computational model \(\mathfrak M\), and an initialization budget function \(B(P)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A boundary definition for feasible-start self-concordant path following. It distinguishes mathematical existence from certified computational access.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A start is missing when \(\mathcal N_\beta(t_0)=\varnothing\) for every admissible initial parameter \(t_0\) allowed by the selected path formulation. A start is inaccessible in model \(\mathfrak M\) and budget \(B\) when such a neighborhood is nonempty but no declared initialization algorithm is certified to output \(x_0\in\mathcal N_\beta(t_0)\) using at most \(B(P)\) charged operations. Equivalently, define \(K_{\mathrm{start}}(P)=+\infty\) when no certified initialization procedure exists in the selected model; the tracking complexity is then only conditional.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A path start is missing if the selected formulation has no point satisfying its initial central-neighborhood requirements. It is inaccessible when qualifying points exist mathematically but no certified procedure can construct one within the declared computational budget. In the latter case, the path-tracking theorem remains a conditional statement and the end-to-end starting cost is treated as infinite or undefined.
assumptions_latex: The allowed initial parameters, target neighborhood, computational model, and charged operations are fixed in advance.
Accessibility refers to certified output, not merely existential knowledge that an interior point exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{Missing}(P)\iff\forall t_0\in T_0,\ \mathcal N_\beta(t_0)=\varnothing;\qquad \operatorname{Inaccessible}_{\mathfrak M,B}(P)\iff\exists t_0\in T_0:\mathcal N_\beta(t_0)\neq\varnothing\ \wedge\ K_{\mathrm{start}}(P)>B(P).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: An inaccessible analytic center may be expressed by \(\inf_{x\in\operatorname{dom}F}\|\nabla F(x)\|_x^*\leq\beta\) together with the absence of a certified algorithm producing such an \(x\).
special_cases_latex: If a verified interior point is supplied, a shifted barrier or auxiliary path may make initialization accessible.
An infeasible-start embedding replaces the original start requirement with a different, explicitly constructible auxiliary start.
immediate_consequences_latex: A feasible-start iteration bound does not apply directly to a missing start.
Existence of an analytic center does not by itself bound the work required to compute an approximate center.
boundary_notes: Inaccessibility is relative to the representation, oracle, computational model, and budget.
An alternative formulation may remove the boundary, but its additional variables and costs must be counted.

notation.meaning: Set of admissible initial path parameters.

children.title: Iteration Complexity versus Oracle Complexity
children.top_down_role: Failure of iteration bounds alone to establish computational tractability.

assumptions_latex: For requested accuracy \(\varepsilon>0\), an algorithm performs \(M(\varepsilon)\) iterations or specified oracle calls, where \(M(\varepsilon)\leq N(\varepsilon)\).
The nonnegative cost of the \(k\)-th performed call is \(C_k\), and all other costs total \(C_{\mathrm{aux}}\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\mathrm{total}}(\varepsilon)=C_{\mathrm{aux}}+\sum_{k=1}^{M(\varepsilon)}C_k\); therefore \(N(\varepsilon)\) alone is not a computational-complexity bound without a cost and representation model.

notation.meaning: Actual and upper-bounded numbers of performed iterations or oracle calls
Cost of the k-th performed oracle call or linear solve

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes the number of path-following steps from the work required to implement them.

source_refs.locator: §1.1.3, “Complexity Bounds for Global Optimization,” p. 10

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If an algorithm performs \(M(\varepsilon)\leq N(\varepsilon)\) iterations or specified oracle calls before producing an \(\varepsilon\)-accurate output, then its work in the declared cost model is
\[
C_{\mathrm{total}}(\varepsilon)=C_{\mathrm{aux}}+\sum_{k=1}^{M(\varepsilon)}C_k.
\]
Thus an iteration bound becomes a computational bound only after the oracle, arithmetic, linear-solve, and representation costs are bounded. In particular, polynomial growth of \(N(\varepsilon)\) in the declared input-size and accuracy parameters establishes polynomial-time tractability only when these per-step and representation costs are also polynomially bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial iteration count establishes tractability only when the declared oracle, linear-solve, arithmetic, and representation costs are polynomially bounded as well.
knowledge_statements.title: Iteration Complexity versus Oracle Complexity

source_witnesses.locator: §1.1.3, “Complexity Bounds for Global Optimization,” p. 10

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Iteration, oracle, arithmetic, and bit complexity
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an algorithm generate \(K(P,\epsilon)\) path-following iterations on instance \(P\). At iteration \(k\), let \(q_{j,k}\) be the number of calls to oracle type \(j\), let \(C_{j,k}\) be the charged cost per such call, and let \(L_k\) be the cost of assembling and solving the Newton system.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic worst-case accounting. The definition applies to exact real-arithmetic, arithmetic-operation, and bit models only after their charged primitives are separately declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Iteration complexity is \(K_{\mathrm{iter}}(P,\epsilon)=K(P,\epsilon)\). Oracle complexity is the vector \(Q_j(P,\epsilon)=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}q_{j,k}\), or its charged total \(C_{\mathrm{oracle}}=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\sum_jq_{j,k}C_{j,k}\). End-to-end computational complexity is \(C_{\mathrm{total}}=C_{\mathrm{start}}+\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}(L_k+\sum_jq_{j,k}C_{j,k})+C_{\mathrm{cert}}\). An iteration bound establishes polynomial computational tractability only when every charged term and the numerical representation lengths are themselves polynomially bounded in the chosen input-size and accuracy measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iteration complexity counts outer path corrections. Oracle complexity counts evaluations of barriers, derivatives, constraints, or other declared primitives. Total computational complexity additionally includes initialization, Newton-system assembly and solution, certification, and—under a bit model—the representation lengths of intermediate quantities. A polynomial iteration count alone is therefore not a polynomial-time guarantee unless all per-iteration and numerical costs are polynomially controlled.
assumptions_latex: The computational model and input-size measure are fixed.
All oracle types and charged linear-algebra, initialization, and certification operations are declared.
For bit complexity, operand lengths and approximation tolerances are included in the accounting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[K_{\mathrm{iter}}=K,\quad Q_j=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}q_{j,k},\quad C_{\mathrm{total}}=C_{\mathrm{start}}+\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\left(L_k+\sum_jq_{j,k}C_{j,k}\right)+C_{\mathrm{cert}},\] and \(K_{\mathrm{iter}}\in\operatorname{poly}\) does not imply \(C_{\mathrm{total}}\in\operatorname{poly}\) without polynomial bounds on the remaining terms.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Newton complexity counts path corrections, whereas arithmetic complexity weights each correction by the operations required to assemble and solve its Newton system.
Bit complexity further weights arithmetic by operand length and required precision.
special_cases_latex: If every iteration uses a constant number of unit-cost oracle calls and \(L_k\leq\operatorname{poly}(|P|)\), a polynomial iteration bound yields a polynomial arithmetic bound.
In a real-arithmetic model, exact real operations have unit cost; this does not automatically imply a bit bound.
immediate_consequences_latex: A \(O(\sqrt\nu\log(1/\epsilon))\) correction bound may coexist with expensive or unavailable derivative oracles.
Structured linear algebra can reduce arithmetic cost without changing the iteration bound.
boundary_notes: Wall-clock complexity also depends on implementation and hardware and is not defined here.
Oracle complexity is meaningless until the oracle's inputs, outputs, and charged cost are specified.

notation.meaning: Number of calls to oracle type \(j\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A complexity theorem proved for a specified short-step update covers only sequences satisfying its hypotheses, including \(x_k\in\operatorname{int}Q\), \(\lambda_{t_k}(x_k)\leq\beta\), the prescribed progress in \(t_k\), and its cost model. A long-step, predictor–corrector, infeasible-start, scaled, or differently inexact method is not covered solely because it uses the same barrier. The variant inherits the bound only after it establishes the required neighborhood preservation, parameter progress, and bounded implementation cost; otherwise the short-step theorem supplies no complexity conclusion for that variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A short-step complexity theorem does not automatically cover algorithmic variants; a variant must establish the theorem's required centrality, progress, and cost conditions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundary between abstract short-step theory and interior-point variants
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Represent an interior-point algorithm by an attribute tuple \(A=(\mathcal N,\sigma,\alpha,\mathcal D,\mathcal F_0,\mathcal S,\mathcal E)\): neighborhood, centering rule, step-length rule, direction equations, start-feasibility regime, scaling, and implementation-error model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification relative to the canonical feasible-start, exact, short-step path-following specification. Being outside this class does not mean that a variant lacks its own convergence or complexity theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the canonical short-step class \(\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{SS}}\) by the predicates: \(\mathcal N\) is the theorem's narrow central neighborhood; \(\sigma=1-\Theta(\nu^{-1/2})\); \(\alpha=1\); \(\mathcal D\) is the declared Newton linearization; the start satisfies the theorem's strict-feasibility and centrality conditions; and \(\mathcal E\) is exact or is covered by an explicit inexactness theorem. The interior-point variant boundary is \(\partial\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{SS}}=\{A:\text{at least one predicate fails or changes}\}\). Long-step line searches, predictor-corrector alternation, infeasible-start residual dynamics, alternative primal-dual scalings, and unverified implementation heuristics lie across this boundary and require their own statements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The canonical short-step class fixes a narrow neighborhood, a conservative square-root-barrier centering change, full steps, a specified Newton system, a certified feasible central start, and an exact or separately justified error model. Changing any of these defining attributes creates a distinct interior-point variant. Long-step, predictor-corrector, infeasible-start, scaling, and implementation choices therefore do not automatically inherit the canonical short-step theorem.
assumptions_latex: A candidate algorithm has a well-defined attribute tuple \(A\).
The reference short-step theorem fixes each comparison predicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[A\in\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{SS}}\iff B_{\mathcal N}(A)\wedge B_\sigma(A)\wedge B_\alpha(A)\wedge B_{\mathcal D}(A)\wedge B_{\mathcal F_0}(A)\wedge B_{\mathcal E}(A);\qquad A\in\partial\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{SS}}\iff\neg(A\in\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{SS}}).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Variant identity is equality of the theorem-relevant algorithmic attributes, not merely use of an interior barrier or Newton direction.
special_cases_latex: A long-step method changes both the neighborhood and step-length rule.
A predictor-corrector method alternates direction and centering roles rather than using one fixed short-step correction.
An infeasible-start method changes the state space and tracks feasibility residuals together with complementarity.
immediate_consequences_latex: A complexity constant or neighborhood-invariance result cannot be transferred solely because two methods share the same central path.
Implementation heuristics require verification against the hypotheses of an applicable variant theorem.
boundary_notes: The boundary is theorem-relative: a method outside \(\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{SS}}\) may belong to another rigorously analyzed class.
Primal and primal-dual path-following methods may use different state variables and direction equations.

notation.meaning: Canonical exact feasible-start short-step algorithm class.
Algorithms differing in at least one theorem-relevant attribute.
